#2206. Leicester City should hand escape route to Hull City player in January: Opinion

Leicester City are eyeing an immediate promotion back from League One to the Championship this season under the guidance of head coach Russell Martin. LCFC slipped out of the second tier earlier this year after they finished in the bottom three along with Sheffield Wednesday and Oxford United.

The Foxes should target a move for Hull City attacking midfielder Kieran Dowell this winter to boost their chances of going up. The Merseyside-born man is expected to leave the Tigers after being left out of their 25-man squad in the Premier League.

Dowell, 29, has played only once for the East Yorkshire outfit in the Carabao Cup so far in this campaign and a change of scene will do him good. He is out of contract at the MKM Stadium in June next year after they handed him an 18-month deal last January when he signed.

Dowell would give Leicester City more competition and depth in their attacking department. He could also inject more quality into LCFC’s squad.

He played with Foxes’ midfielder John Lundstram at Hull City last term. The pair helped the Tigers win the play-offs and reach the top flight against the odds.

Dowell’s game time has dried up under Sergej Jakirovic since then though and he is now surplus to requirements. He was offered to Sheffield United in the summer but nothing materialised on that front in the end and he stayed put beyond the last deadline.

The ex-England youth international is available now though and landing him would be a statement of intent by Leicester City if they managed to get him. He will surely have interest from the division above but the prospect of regular minutes could turn his head.

Dowell had a spell in League One with Birmingham City in 2025. He helped the Blues win the title under Chris Davies.

Therefore, he knows what it takes to get out of Leicester City’s league. His experience would come in very handy for LCFC and he would be a useful character to have in and around the dressing room.

Dowell rose up through Everton’s academy as a youngster. He has also had stints at Sheffield United, Derby County, Norwich City, Wigan Athletic, Norwich City and Rangers.

A deal wouldn’t break the bank, and it could give Russell Martin a valuable extra creative spark.

#2205. Taylor, non solo il tacco: i numeri della sua gara con la Lazio contro il Lecce

All’assist per Noslin si aggiungono due primati: 12,203 chilometri percorsi e 17 passaggi riusciti nell’ultimo terzo.

L’assist di tacco per Noslin è la giocata che resta negli occhi. Un’intuizione che impreziosisce la prestazione di Kenneth Taylor contro il Lecce e contribuisce al successo della Lazio. Il suo pomeriggio, però, offre molto altro da raccontare oltre al gesto tecnico del raddoppio. laziopress.itL’olandese chiude con 12,203 chilometri percorsi e 17 passaggi riusciti nell’ultimo terzo di campo: in entrambe le voci è il primo tra tutti i giocatori della partita. A questi numeri aggiunge due passaggi chiave, completando una prova nella quale impegno fisico e partecipazione alla manovra offensiva si accompagnano.È soprattutto l’incrocio tra i due primati a offrire una chiave di lettura della sua gara: Taylor dà continuità al lavoro del centrocampo e partecipa allo sviluppo del possesso nella zona più vicina alla porta avversaria.Taylor, 12,203 chilometri: il lavoro oltre l’assistIl dato sulla distanza percorsa restituisce la dimensione quantitativa della prestazione.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Nessun altro giocatore del match corre quanto Taylor, che termina la sfida superando i dodici chilometri.La distanza, da sola, non permette di stabilire quanto siano stati efficaci i singoli movimenti, né di distinguere il lavoro offensivo da quello difensivo. Documenta però un impegno prolungato, che affianca la qualità mostrata nell’azione dell’assist.Il tacco diventa così il momento più appariscente di una partita sostenuta anche da un volume di corsa superiore a quello di tutti gli altri protagonisti.Diciassette passaggi riusciti nell’ultimo terzoL’altro primato riguarda i 17 passaggi completati nell’ultimo terzo. Un numero che mette a fuoco la partecipazione di Taylor al possesso nella zona offensiva.Sono palloni arrivati a destinazione nella porzione di campo in cui la Lazio cerca di sviluppare e rifinire le proprie azioni. Il dato sostiene quindi la lettura di un centrocampista coinvolto nel collegamento con l’attacco, capace di contribuire alla continuità della manovra avanzata.

#2203. 'Managers now are b****y boring!': NEIL WARNOCK on the lack of characters in football, his friendship with Pep Guardiola, why he is open to managing again post-Christmas - and how he almost became a chiropodist!

Published: 19:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 08:25 EST, 16 November 2026

Spending time in the company of Neil Warnock is always an education, be it witnessing one of his legendary foul-mouthed touchline rants or perched at one of his stage shows at grand venues like London Palladium.

On this occasion, Daily Mail Sport is perched in an east London bar watching on as one of English football's national treasures is posing for some modelling. Yes, you read that right, Mr Warnock is here to launch his own pair of socks with a tipple of Famous Grouse whisky in hand.

The complements on Warnock's 77-year-old feet are soon over, though, and we can get on to talking about a life in football that started six decades ago as a winger for Chesterfield and has traversed 10 clubs as a player, 17 as a manager and more than 2,000 games in the dugout.

So where to start? Maybe his reflections on nearly five decades in management – and how the whole conversation about feet is not too out of place…

'You don't realise how long it has been really, I started off just a team of ragamuffins as I call them,' he says in his iconic Yorkshire accent. 'They used to train on the green where I had digs in Hartlepool and asked me to coach them.

'I remember we scored from a set-piece we worked on, I was running up and down the touchline high-fiving everyone. I got the bug. I knew I could never get to the top as a player, I was quick but I was brainless.

Daily Mail Sport caught up with Neil Warnock to discuss his six decades in football

After representing 10 different clubs as a player, Warnock became one of the most compelling managers in the game

'I could've been a chiropodist if not in football. That could be on a quiz, couldn't it? I had bad feet at Scunthorpe, I used to get massive blisters so the physio there started getting me to do some of the players' feet.

'I enjoyed doing ingrown toenails and things like that! So I thought why not? Then I had a practice in Sheffield. I had to make a decision when we won the league at Scarborough whether to go full-time or pack it in. I thought, "Oh, go on then, let's give it a little go".

'It's not worked out badly, really, has it?

'People come up to me every day and say, "You're a legend, you". And I say, "Oh, thank you very much". Then they tell me what club they support, I have had so many haven't I? Last week I went out for a minute and had four selfies. They all appreciate what I did for their club.

'There aren't as many characters in the game now, you wouldn't get upset with managers now like in my day because now they are that b****y boring! Some of them barely speak.

'They won't get the rapport we had. I managed at a good time. The way I managed, I needed that humour. I needed the lads to enjoy it. I signed a lot of players that many managers wouldn't touch with a barge pole, are you with me? They ended up getting me promotions.'

The aforementioned humour brings us on to a private conversation he had with the great Pep Guardiola, one of the millions of anecdotes up Warnock's sleeve but one that he has not told until now.

'I went to a training session and he asked me to say a few words,' explains Warnock. 'I said, "Well lads I bet you're glad I'm not your manager because we'd be kicking balls from there to there, chasing it, heading it, practicing our tackles"... everyone laughed.

Warnock views Pep Guardiola as the best manager of his lifetime, while the Spaniard praised the veteran's humour after once addressing his Man City squad at a training session

Warnock has led teams to promotions on eight occasions over the course of his career

'After the session we had a coffee and Pep said to me, "Neil, that was amazing, you know when you talked to the players? I understood why you had so many promotions".

'He started counting and said, "What we have is all these staff… computers, details, nutritionist, all these staff, but you know what we don't have? Humour". He noticed why my lads had done well in my teams, just in that meeting. It was good, that. He is amazing.

'Pep is the best manager of my lifetime. They say he had all the best players but it is not easy managing them. Pep did things with players and now there are non-league teams trying to play like Manchester City!'

Warnock is now doing stage tours - Guardiola attended one last season - and had a tear in his eye when he stepped out at London Palladium given he used to watch shows there with his mother, who was in a wheelchair, on the TV as a child.

So what is Warnock up to these days? His current role is advisor at Torquay United but last management job was at Aberdeen two years ago… so is he out of the rat race for good this time?

'No, not really, no,' he says. 'I only work from February to April! So the phone will be on after Christmas. You never know, do ya? There will be someone thinking "why don't we get that Warnock in?".

'I've retired 40 times! Every time I have said it, I have meant it. But it's that dressing room camaraderie. There's something about football, when I look at some of the managers now… they just don't excite me.

'I remember Ruben Amorim (breaks down laughing). He's got his computer out on the bench! I remember watching and thinking, "I'm sorry, son, you need more than a computer to help you tonight!".

Warnock is currently doing stage tours, with Guardiola among the attendees last season

Warnock's current role is advisor at Torquay United and briefly served as interim manager last season, with the 77-year-old admitting he had not completely ruled out a return to the dugout

'And likewise, I see them making notes on the bench, oh my god. I think "what are you doing, your shopping list for Tescos?".

'I do enjoy walking and I enjoy photography, believe it or not. I go up the river with my phone, there's so many lovely things to see.

'I've got an electric bike and I sometimes do about 25 miles. I was thinking of doing a cycle of all my clubs but that would take me five years! They go at about 30mph down the hills, you've got to be careful, you wouldn't want to come off them.'

He is also enjoying fishing, being with the family and playing golf with his son, a PGA rising star William - though Warnock Sr insists he often embarrasses himself playing off 'the ladies' tee'.

The thing that makes Warnock most proud is the four promotions at Wembley but also the togetherness he fostered in his many teams.

He tells us: 'What I like about the teams I had, they all have reunions. You look at the tele now, someone will score a goal and kiss the badge… they won't have a reunion.

'When I go to these reunions, I see all my lads and how I blended that dressing room together and I look at the comradeship they still have now, they are the same as they were just a lot older.

'This year, my Scarborough team are having a 40-year celebration and the lads have invited me. I said there's no way I'm going out with that lot after the do because they can drink, let me tell you!'

#2201. 3 left-backs West Ham must eye as after Scott Parker makes January transfer demands

West Ham must first navigate a busy December schedule before the January transfer window opens, but Scott Parker is already planning to strengthen his squad. The Hammers boss has identified two key positions he wants to address, with a new striker and left-back both on his January wish list.

The left-back role has been an issue for WHU this season after the departure of El Hadji Malick Diouf. Academy duo Ezra Mayers and Ollie Scarles have had opportunities in that role but have failed to nail down the spot.

Adama Boiro was brought in late in the summer window but he has managed just 13 minutes of league action since his arrival. There only other option in that role has been Morato but he is a natural centre-back.

With that said, here are three left-backs that could solve Scott Parker’s issues at West Ham…

Harrison Burrows brings a different, more attacking dimension from left-back. At Sheffield United he has posted strong goal and assist numbers while operating as a left-back or wing-back, showing he can contribute in the final third as well as defend.

That end product is useful for a West Ham side that needs more threat from deeper areas. Energetic in the press and capable of overlapping or underlapping, he adds balance to a back line that has often lacked a specialist left-sided option.

While he has no prior Parker connection, his Championship pedigree and creative output make him a sensible complementary target alongside more defensively oriented options. He would give Parker a player who can both protect and progress.

Lucas Pires stands out because of his direct experience under Parker. During Burnley’s 2024/25 Championship promotion campaign he was a regular starter at left-back, logging a high number of appearances in a side that prioritised defensive organisation and controlled possession.

That familiarity with Parker’s demands is valuable for West Ham, who are still bedding in a new system. At Championship level he has shown reliability in one-v-one defending, solid positioning and the ability to recycle possession calmly.

Still only in his mid-twenties and currently at Burnley, he represents a realistic, modest-fee option rather than a high-risk gamble. His prior success in Parker’s set-up reduces the adaptation period and gives West Ham a proven, system-ready left-back who has already contributed to a promotion.

Harry Amass offers a high-upside profile that fits a promotion-chasing side. At 19 he has already accumulated meaningful Championship minutes on loan at Sheffield Wednesday and Norwich City, demonstrating he can handle the physical and technical demands of the division.

Athletic, left-footed and comfortable stepping into midfield, he provides both defensive cover and progressive carrying from the back. Limited first-team opportunities at Manchester United make a permanent or long-term move plausible, and he has been repeatedly linked with West Ham.

For Parker, Amass represents a younger, more dynamic alternative who can grow into the role over multiple seasons while still delivering immediate Championship quality. His age, athletic traits and proven second-tier experience make him an attractive, future-proof target.

#2198. 220-appearance star still without a club after summer departure from Leicester City

Leicester City’s rapid decline from the Premier League to League One means there has been a lot of change over the past two years. LCFC’s place as European football contenders is a thing of the past, and so are many of the players.

Among the mainstays in the Foxes’ Premier League days was right-back Ricardo Pereira, who joined from FC Porto in 2018 and grew into a starring role at the King Power Stadium. He was one of the league’s best in his position, but injuries hit and limited his involvement.

Pereira stayed throughout Leicester City’s yo-yo years, but when his contract came to an end earlier this year, it was decided that he would move on. And, over four months on from his release, he remains out of the game.

Pereira managed 39 appearances in Leicester City’s relegation season, proving he can still manage a demanding season despite previous injury issues.

His pedigree at the very top of the game with the Foxes and Porto has seen him grow into a leadership figure over the years. The experience he has to his name is of huge value to younger players and his character would quickly see him become an influential figure in the dressing room.

Granted, the speed and physical traits Pereira showed at his best aren’t as strong anymore. However, he has always been a technically gifted player in possession, and his pedigree helps him read the game well.

Pereira has shared images and videos of himself training during his time without a team. He would need time to get up to speed to play full games at a competitive level, but he has kept himself ticking over as he awaits his next opportunity after leaving LCFC.

It remains to be seen just what awaits Pereira after a long spell out of the game. Opportunities do dry up as the season moves on from the summer transfer window, so there might not be many intriguing options out there.

The MLS regular season has just ended, so the Leicester City man could join a team for their 2027 preparations to be ready to go for the new campaign. Alternatively though, Pereira may wish to see out the latter years of his career back in his home country of Portugal.

Teams in Liga Portugal would certainly benefit from his leadership and experience. Having broken through in his home country before leaving for bigger things, it could be a fitting end to his career to return and become an influential player for a top flight side.

14:30 – Inizia la ripresa, batte la Lazio

39′ – Occasione Napoli allo scadere: cross dalla sinistra, sul secondo palo arriva Maglio in corsa, ma era molto defilato, il suo pallonetto finisce alto

22′ – Occasione per il Napoli: cross basso dalla destra, e dopo un rimpallo, Ciotola calcia di prima intenzione, il suo tiro finisce alto

17′ – Ammonito il tecnico della Lazio Gualdaroni per proteste

16′ – Doppia occasione per la Lazio: cross dalla destra, Spoletini colpisce di testa, ma respinge Mataluna. Sulla ribattuta ancora Spoletini ci prova, ma Mataluna mette in corner

4′ – Contropiede del Napoli: Tambaro porta via il pallone centralmente, poi scarica a Ciotola in area, che calcia a botta sicura, la Lazio salva sulla linea

3′ – Ripartenza dal basso sbagliata della Lazio, Maglio recupera palla dal limite ma calcia sul fondo

#2196. Paredes sviene durante l’intervista dopo il trionfo del Boca

Il centrocampista si è ripreso in pochi minuti; lo staff medico lo ha portato in una clinica di Barranquilla.

Leandro Paredes è svenuto durante un’intervista con DSports dopo il trionfo nella Copa Sudamericana con il Boca Juniors. Secondo quanto riportato da Sportal, Il centrocampista argentino, ex Juventus e Roma, stava rispondendo a una domanda del cronista quando è crollato improvvisamente.

Paredes è stato soccorso immediatamente e si è ripreso nel giro di pochi minuti. Lo staff medico del Boca Juniors ha comunque preferito trasportarlo in una clinica di Barranquilla per degli accertamenti. L’allarme è rientrato presto.

In seguito, il centrocampista ha rassicurato tutti sui social: «Sto bene: viva il Boca, oggi e sempre». Ha poi ringraziato per i messaggi ricevuti e spiegato l’accaduto: «Grazie a tutti per i messaggi: è stato solo un giramento di testa dovuto a tutti quei festeggiamenti».

#2195. Monza, Varela via? Juric: "Se vendiamo a 40-50 milioni e li riutilizziamo per me è un bene"

Ivan Juric, tecnico del Monza, è intervenuto in conferenza stampa alla vigilia della partita contro la Fiorentina e ha parlato anche di Gustavo Varela e della possibile cessione dei giovani calciatori a metà campionato: "L’obiettivo è rimanere in serie A con questi principi, e quindi ragazzi giovani. Se vendi qualcuno a 40-50 milioni come mi è successo a Verona e Torino e li riutilizzi in maniera intelligente per me è un bene. I margini di miglioramento sono impressionanti. Secondo me ha fatto la sua miglior prestazione contro l'Atalanta".

Rientrerà qualcuno? "Maye, Folorunsho e Ngonge non ci saranno, mentre Ziolkowski sarà a disposizione. Mi chiedete se giocherà Birindelli o Toure… Mi piacciono entrambi, ho due giocatori che mi fanno sentir sereno. Pessina ha fatto due settimane di allenamento. Solo la sua presenza alza il livello dell'allenamento. Domani titolare? Ci penserò".

Quanto è cresciuto il suo Monza? "Siamo migliorati tantissimo, noto una crescita immensa anche a partire dall'ultima contro l'Atalanta. Il morale è molto alto. Non siamo soddisfatti a livello di classifica, ma come prestazioni sì. Dobbiamo andare avanti per la nostra strada senza deprimerci. La Fiorentina ha una squadra importantissima, hanno fatto un sacco di acquisti. Andiamo a giocare con grandissimo coraggio e dovremo essere perfetti".

#2194. Wolves must look to sanction an exit for £10m prospect in the January transfer window: Opinion

Wolves have long looked overseas for new stars to bring into their ranks. Some go straight into the first team, like current aces Andre, while others develop in the academy or out on loan before coming into the fold at Molineux.

Paraguayan winger Enso Gonzalez has primarily played academy football since joining from Club Libertad in 2023. He broke into the senior game in his native country and caught the eye, but to date, he has made just one appearance for the Old Gold’s first team.

Gonzalez will turn 22 in January, and the fact he has not been involved in a single senior matchday squad this season indicates he isn’t close to breaking into Cesar Peixoto‘s plans. To aid his development, Wolves must explore exit options for the winger in the winter window.

Gonzalez joined Wolves aged 18 after impressing in Paraguay. Upon arrival, former sporting director Matt Hobbs said: “He’s an exciting, young player, who will fit in well with our dressing room and within the DNA we’re trying to create. We wanted a front player who could play across the line and give us something different, and Enso is the name our recruitment team pushed.

“His creativity stood out, playing forward, being aggressive in possession and doing his work out of possession, but for me it was more what he does offensively.”

But, despite the clear hopes that Gonzalez could break through at Molineux, he has not found anywhere near the role he hoped for. He has shown sparks in the U21s with four goals in 12 games this season; however it doesn’t appear to have got him any closer to Peixoto’s side.

This lack of progression through the ranks is stunting his development. Wanderers must take action to chance Gonzalez’s trajectory in January, unless it goes down as £10m wasted by the club.

Gonzalez is playing, so he’s retaining sharpness and staying active. But, in terms of progress, there really isn’t much for a player of his age to gain from playing the likes of Fleetwood Town’s U21s in the Premier League Cup, or Wealdstone in the National League Cup.

If Wolves are to maximise his potential, Gonzalez has to be sent out on loan. He needs to go and play first-team football at a good level so they can gauge whether he has a future at Molineux.

Alternatively, if the club already feel that his chances of a breakthrough are slim, all parties will benefit from a sale. Wanderers can cut their losses, and Gonzalez can take his talents elsewhere in the bid to kick on.

Regardless of the structure of the deal, Gonzalez needs a move away from Wolves.

#2190. England's evolution: James Trafford and two other stars chisel their names into the XI, Thomas Tuchel learning from Argentina and Jude Bellingham playing like a captain!

Published: 02:32 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:25 EST, 16 November 2026

England ended world champions Spain's 43-match unbeaten run in dramatic fashion with a 3-2 win on a memorable night in Madrid.

After Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White scored to establish a three-goal lead, the visitors had to cling on after Elliot Anderson was sent off and the hosts scored twice in the final half hour.

The victory means Thomas Tuchel's side top their Nations League group and it provided a strong riposte to criticism of the manager following the World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in July.

Our chief football reporter, Craig Hope, was at the Metropolitano Stadium, and here are his FIVE big take-aways…

It would not have mattered had England conceded a late equaliser. To draw comparison with Argentina in the final half hour is unfair and inaccurate. The World Cup semi-final was 11v11 and so, when we draw conclusions from this game, let us do so on the same terms.

Thomas Tuchel was delighted with his England players as they won 3-2 away in Spain

And what did England do at 11v11 with a 1-0 lead? They attacked. And attacked again. This was a major change (and improvement) and is the reason for such encouragement. They have learnt from a mistake, as much as Tuchel will be loathe to admit.

Mexico would be a fairer parallel, but that was against opposition far inferior to Spain. At 11v10, we could not expect England to stay on the front foot here, as they were until the point of Jarell Quansah's needless mistake and Elliot Anderson's subsequent red card.

And that is cause for great optimism - because this game was not in the balance in any way when the teams were at equal number.

For me, and I don't think this is even close, this was the best performance of Tuchel's reign.

Do England suddenly have a pair of full backs?! After years of trawling and trialling, here in the most testing of surrounds, Ben White and Lewis Hall inked their names into Tuchel's XI.

We can forgive the concession of two goals when down to 10 men - because with 11, Spain barely looked like getting a shot on target. In fact, they didn't.

Much of that was down to the solidity of the full backs. Then, with backs to the wall, the pair became bricks in the resistance. One White block late on was heroic.

Before that, Hall's best work was not in containing Lamine Yamal, but in emulating him. His dribbles were daring and unnerved Spain, who thought they would spend the game in England's half and with the ball. They did neither early on and Hall was central to that.

White's goal had shades of Carlos Alberto on the overlap, and his England redemption arc felt like it reached completion here. Let him now move on now, for England need him.

No more boos, please, only cheers for White (and Hall).

It's time to stop the boos for Ben White after he starred with Lewis Hall at full back

Ezri Konsa is England's best defender. Build the backline around him.

Tuchel said on the eve of the game that he thought Konsa had grown for the move to Arsenal, and this was proof.

Boy do England need a mature, reliable presence at the heart of their defence. Konsa showed here why he can be that man. He scored a fine goal, which is always a sign of a defender ready to take wider responsibility, but it was his cool interceptions and desperate blocks at the other end that were most reassuring.

What Konsa has to do now is build on this - and a man-of-the-match performance at the home of the world champions is a pretty lofty and solid foundation from which to do so.

Tuchel will, and should, be giving serious thought to keeping James Trafford in England's goal for the Nations League quarter-finals.

Jordan Pickford has done nothing wrong. And yet, it feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and here was his justification.

Trafford can be a little erratic and immature. What better way to grow, emotionally, than with a series of saves to preserve an historic win. He will feel like a different player, and person, to the one who started this game. Like White and Hall, this felt like a coming-of-age night in an England jersey.

Trafford has all the tools. He might just have used them to chisel his name into that team-sheet.

Goalkeeper feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and James Trafford starred

Spain's fans are left shocked as Ezri Konsa hails the brilliant Trafford in emphatic fashion

No goals, but England would not have won this game without Bellingham. He terrified Spain, perhaps given their intimate knowledge of his brilliance.

Beating the best is as much a mental challenge as it is physical, and Bellingham believed. He made England believe, too.

His swagger. His majesty. And yes, his skill. Of all the positives from this win, it is hard to look past Bellingham as the biggest reason for England being able to challenge Spain at the top of the world rankings.

Jude Bellingham played like a captain, dropping into midfield when down to 10 men

He won the corner for the second goal and created the third. He then dropped into midfield when down to 10 and played like a captain.

That is what England need - Bellingham the leader, not Bellingham the individual. He has bought into the collective under Tuchel and, with that, his team-mates are buying into his big ideas. They don't come much bigger than what England achieved here.

#2189. Four goals in four games: £8m ex-Middlesbrough man’s fine form fails to save new club from dramatic collapse

Middlesbrough had a busy summer transfer window as they prepared for the 2026/27 campaign. Boro struck big-money deals for the likes of Will Lankshear, Radek Vitek and Ashley Phillips in their hunt for redemption after Championship play-off final heartbreak in May.

However, there were departures from the Riverside Stadium too; some more surprising than others. Among the moves to raise eyebrows across the EFL was Morgan Whittaker’s sale to Colorado Rapids for a reported fee of around £8m.

The 25-year-old scored 14 goals and provided seven assists in 40 Championship games last season. As such, it was a little surprising to see him move for a fee barely over the £7.5m package sum paid to sign him from Plymouth Argyle in January 2025.

Whittaker quickly caught the eye in the United States. In his first MLS start back in September, the former Middlesbrough man netted a brace in Colorado Rapids’ 3-3 draw against Seattle Sounders.

He would then go four games without a goal before really hitting his stride in October. Whittaker would score in four consecutive games against Vancouver Whitecaps, San Jose Earthquakes, Chicago Fire and FC Dallas to take him to six goals in 10 league games for the Rapids.

Unfortunately, despite Whittaker’s form, the side desperately struggled for results. Of those 10 appearances, Colorado only won twice, and it ultimately cost them a place in the MLS play-offs.

They sat in 8th on the final day, which would have been enough to qualify. However, Whittaker’s goal against Dallas was his side’s only one in a 3-1 defeat, seeing Colorado slip to 13th and completely out of play-off contention.

It marked the second time in consecutive years that the Rapids have missed out on the play-offs on the final day.

It was a surprise to see Whittaker swap Middlesbrough for Colorado Rapids, especially given the finances of the deal weren’t too eye-catching. However, it marked an exciting opportunity for the forward to go and play in the MLS, and his goalscoring qualities have certainly been on show.

At 25, he still has plenty of time to develop and reach higher levels too. Impressive form in America combined with his strong Championship track record means Whittaker could certainly earn a switch to a bigger league in the years to come.

It would not be a surprise to see Whittaker plying his trade on English shores again. For now though, he’ll take time to rest up in the MLS off-season before attacking the 2027 campaign with a vengeance.

#2188. Verso Torino-Lazio, l'infermeria granata tiene in dubbio due titolari

Le parole di Abate nel post-partita con il Napoli accendono i riflettori sulle condizioni di Belghali e Ismajli verso la sfida contro i biancocelesti; stop muscolare pure per Biraghi.

In vista della sfida di sabato 28 novembre alle 18:00, valida per la 13ª giornata di Serie A, che vedrà i biancocelesti impegnati nella trasferta sul campo del Torino, le condizioni fisiche in casa granata assumono un peso specifico notevole per la Lazio, chiamata a guardare con attenzione alle possibili assenze emerse dopo la gara con il Napoli.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Al termine della partita di ieri sera contro i partenopei, il tecnico Abate ha fatto chiarezza sulle condizioni di due elementi della rosa: "Belghali si porta dietro un problema al ginocchio da settimane, Ismajli potrebbe essersi rotto un dito della mano". Due situazioni da valutare giorno per giorno che interessano da vicino anche la Lazio: Belghali stava attraversando un ottimo momento di forma prima dello stop, mentre Ismajli si è fin qui dimostrato il più affidabile e brillante del terzetto difensivo granata. La loro assenza sarebbe un duro colpo per il Torino nella sfida contro i biancocelesti.

Sempre dopo la sfida con il Napoli, l'allenatore granata ha aggiunto un ulteriore aggiornamento chiave per la preparazione della Lazio: "Biraghi ha avuto un affaticamento". Un problema muscolare che impone cautela in settimana per evitare ricadute e che mette a rischio la sua presenza per la 13ª giornata di campionato, togliendo potenzialmente esperienza e spinta sulla fascia ai granata nel confronto con i biancocelesti.

#2185. Bayern Monaco, che spavento: nuova crisi neurologica per Musiala, come sta ora

Non c'è pace per Jamal Musiala e il Bayern Monaco. Secondo quanto riferito da Sky Sports DE, il trequartista tedesco lunedì scorso ha subito nuovamente una crisi neurologica, eppure il 23enne ha potuto partecipare all'allenamento regolarmente poco dopo.

Per Musiala si tratta del secondo episodio nel corso degli ultimi tre mesi. La situazione del giocatore classe 2003 continua a essere monitorata attentamente presso il club bavarese, nonostante però Jamal si sia potuto allenare nella giornata successiva al centro sportivo del Bayern Monaco senza alcun problema o limitazione. Preparativi prima del match contro il Colonia (1-1) in Bundesliga dove ha disputato addirittura 20 minuti in campo.

La terapia farmacologica di Musiala viene adeguata e ottimizzata costantemente, secondo l'emittente satellitare, in stretto coordinamento con i medici del Bayern Monaco. Mentre la situazione viene seguita con preoccupazione soprattutto nel consiglio direttivo e nel consiglio di sorveglianza del club, la valutazione della dirigenza sportiva sarebbe decisamente più positiva. Rochdale have been left 22nd in the League Two table after a seven-game winless run. The dismal streak extended with a 3-2 loss against fellow strugglers Northampton Town on Saturday, putting head coach Ian Watson in real danger.

And, on Sunday morning, it was confirmed that the Dale had parted ways with Watson, who was appointed as Jimmy McNulty‘s replacement on a three-year deal in the summer.

The search for Watson’s replacement has already begun. Here, we put forward three contenders who should be on Rochdale’s radar…

Given his close connection with rivals Bury, Ryan Lowe may not be minded to take the vacant post at Spotland. However, Rochdale need EFL experience after poaching Watson from South Shields didn’t work out, and Lowe would bring that in abundance.

His stint with Wigan Athletic was tough, but he did a steady job over the course of nearly three years at Preston North End and delivered League Two promotion in his time at Plymouth Argyle. He had them 4th in League One when he left for Deepdale too.

Lowe’s EFL pedigree could be just what the Dale need to push away from the drop and further up the table in the long term. His locality ticks a box as well.

Talk around a potential move to Crawley Town has been brought to an end by their appointment of Kevin Blackwell. Woodman could be the leader Rochdale need to ease nerves and move away from the relegation battle. He won 123 of 289 games in charge of the Ravens and could deliver results at Spotland too.

Last but not least is Stuart Maynard, who led Rochdale’s 2025/26 National League promotion rivals York City. His side came out on top in that battle for the title, but the Minstermen surprisingly sacked the 46-year-old before a ball had been kicked in the EFL.

Maynard made a name for himself at Wealdstone before falling short in the League Two play-offs with Notts County. His York City record was fantastic though, proving himself as a boss capable of taking to the next level in impressive fashion.

#2183. 96% pass completion, four chances created: Returning QPR man’s importance shown in 1-0 win over Millwall

QPR continued their strong campaign to date with a triumph over last year’s Championship play-off semi-finalists Millwall. Just one goal was enough to get the job done, as the Hoops claimed all three points.

Zak Sturge was sent off for the Lions early on, and the R’s made their man advantage count. There were solid performances across the board with Ilias Chair impressing in attack, and the displays of defensive trio Ronnie Edwards, Jake Clarke-Salter and Kealey Adamson gave Julien Stephan plenty to smile about.

However, on the day, it was midfielder Nicolas Madsen who stood out. On his return to the starting lineup after a spell out through injury, the Dane was almost faultless in possession and scored the decisive goal for QPR.

Madsen’s goal saw him pounce on a saved shot to side-foot goalwards, and after Mark Sykes’ attempt to clear, referee Josh Smith gave the signal that the ball had indeed crossed the line.

The QPR star was central to Sturge’s red card too. Madsen took one touch before curling a fantastic pass in behind to Paul Smyth, who was bundled over by the Millwall defender.

The numbers behind Madsen’s display are just as eye-catching. He completed 88 of his 92 passes, equating to a success rate of 96%, with 13 of these balls being into the final third and four of them created chances for his Hoops teammates.

No one saw more of the ball than Madsen, who had 102 touches across his 74-minute outing. Millwall’s red card meant they couldn’t threaten much and only recorded 31% possession, but Madsen was on hand to help out defensively when needed with one interception, one clearance, and a 66% duel win rate (all stats via FotMob).

Madsen had not played in over a month due to injury. However, having recorded two goals and an assist in his last two games before being cast to the sidelines, the QPR star picked up right where he left off with a fine performance against Millwall.

With his second-half substitution, Stephan clearly had one eye on his involvement against Norwich City on Saturday. Rightly so, as he will be key in the battle against their strong midfield containing Paris Maghoma, Jacob Wright, Kenny McLean and former Hoops man Sam Field.

Few QPR fans needed a reminder of just how influential Madsen is, but his display against Millwall emphasised his value. He brings goals from midfield, reliability and creativity in possession, and strength in duels when needed.

If the R’s are to maintain their push for the Championship play-offs, Madsen will have a key role to play.

#2182. How Vinicius Jr's lavish summer holiday has left him playing catch up: Real Madrid star admits he 'trained less' while on luxury yacht trip and blames Brazil's early World Cup exit - and 'overwhelming' Arsenal rumours - for sluggish start to the season

Published: 09:07 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:48 EST, 16 November 2026

Vinicius Junior has admitted his lavish summer holiday after Brazil's last-16 World Cup exit is behind his slow start with Real Madrid this season.

And the winger says he felt 'overwhelmed' by the interest of clubs such as Arsenal  and insecurity around his contract renewal talks in Madrid.

He has scored one goal and provided three assists in 12 games this season, and amid the criticism, manager Jose Mourinho has even said he should have left this summer to go somewhere he is 'respected'.

Vini Jr said: 'I don’t think I prepared better after the World Cup because the impact of this tournament is very significant for all Brazilians. Losing so early was something we didn’t expect.

'So I took advantage of the holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in recent years. This may have affected my start to the season.

'Also, regarding my contract renewal, with so many clubs interested last summer, I felt really overwhelmed, as did the situation at Real Madrid. But the season is very long.

Vinicius Junior has admitted his lavish summer holiday is behind his slow start to the season (Instagram: vinijr)

The Real Madrid star spent plenty of time relaxing on yachts as he visited Brazil, Jamaica, Italy, and Dubai (Instagram: vinijr)

The 26-year-old got around via private jet and said that he wants to 'enjoy life' (Instagram: vinijr)

'Maintaining such a high level for so long is always very difficult. I believe only Cristiano Ronaldo and (Lionel) Messi have managed to maintain it for so many years, achieving the same numbers.

'I'm human, I make mistakes often, but I always try to improve. I try to understand more about football, about the day-to-day, but I'm 26 years old and I have to enjoy life a little too.

'Last season, until December, I had only scored five goals. Then, I finished with more than 20 goals, as in all other seasons. I believe I am preparing, evolving, because, in the most decisive moment of the season, I am always there.'

Vini Jr spent part of his summer break in his home city of Sao Goncalo, as well as visiting Jamaica, Italy, and Dubai.

His Instagram was full of pictures of him relaxing on yachts, speeding around on a private jet, and showing off his fashionable outfits.

Arsenal enquired about the Brazilian superstar and reports suggested they were willing to offer him a mammoth £18.5million per season - more than any player at the club.

His contract expires at the end of the season and the club's position is that he must lower his demands if they are to agree an extension. They would still be willing to make him their joint-highest earner alongside Kylian Mbappe.

He has often been a target of racism in Spain - there have been more than 20 such cases of alleged abuse towards him since he joined from Flamengo in 2018. The situation has reduced him to tears before, but he has insisted on staying in La Liga so that he doesn't 'give the racists what they want'.

The winger - who has scored one goal and provided three assists this season - was a target for Arsenal and could leave Madrid in January

The winger is currently serving a four-match ban for pulling Villarreal star Nathan Saliba's hair.

And Mourinho said last month: 'If I were in his shoes, I probably wouldn't be here. I would have forced a move to a country where he'd be respected, but out of loyalty to Real Madrid and love for the club, he stayed.

'He believes things can improve, and he still has that smile. Nothing and no one can take it away from him.

'He's a fantastic guy, and it's easy to get along with him. I spend a few minutes alone with him every day.

'I value him immensely because he always manages to live and survive with a smile.'

Vinicius has been a phenomenon at Real Madrid, scoring 129 times in 388 games from the wing.

But the balance of power shifted to Mbappe when he joined from Paris Saint-Germain in 2024 and talk of his future has increased.

There is a chance that, if Madrid go a third season in a row without significant silverware, they choose to rebuild and go in a different direction.

Moving away from the heavy 'superstar' model has worked for PSG and rewarded them with two Champions League titles in a row.

Vinicius had a tricky summer, being knocked out of the last 16 of the World Cup with Brazil and then missing his pre-season return date as his representatives tried to revive talks over a contract extension.

If an agreement cannot be found on a new deal, Madrid could be open to selling in January, rather than lose him for free next summer.

Last year Al Ahli were willing to offer a €1bn five-year contract offer for the 2024 Ballon d'Or runner-up.

Liverpool were also credited with interest earlier this window but are not in the mix for a player who earns around £520,000 a week.

#2181. 3 managers Watford must target after sacking Alessio Dionisi

Watford were thrashed by Sheffield United on Saturday, putting Alessio Dionisi under new pressure. Now, it has been confirmed that the head coach has been relieved of his duties.

The Hornets had shown a desire to stick by Dionisi, as opposed to their past managerial hire-and-fire approach. But, sitting 21st in the Championship table and after an incredibly defeated post-match press conference on Saturday, change awaits.

Here, we put forward three bosses who Watford should consider in their next head coach hunt…

Watford desperately need a boss who can galvanise this squad. There are talented players like Othmane Maamma, Iker Bravo and Amin Nabizada, but those forwards can only be given freedom to express themselves if the manager instils confidence in the entire team.

Bo Henriksen would do just that. In his managerial career to date, the 51-year-old’s best attribute has been his man management. He encourages his skilful players to express themselves on the ball and leads with emotion and passion, prioritising a unified group over unique and complicated tactics.

He’ll demand intensity in pressing and quick transitions, but what Henriksen could do to this group is where he stands out. The Dane is available after his exit from Mainz in December 2025 and previously succeeded with Bronshoj BK, AC Horsens, FC Midtjylland and FC Zurich.

This may be a slightly hopeful suggestion. However, there is a reason it could work.

Michael O’Neill is currently in charge of the Northern Ireland national side, but he split his role with a stint as Blackburn Rovers boss last season. During that spell, he managed to lead the Lancashire outfit to Championship safety, and given that there is no international football until March, Watford should see if he is open to a similar dual-responsibility position.

The 57-year-old’s teams are well organised and his experience in the dugout means he’s happy to be flexible with his setup too. Like Henriksen, he has been praised for his work as a man manager and could lead a much-needed turnaround at Watford.

His Championship track record is solid too. If he can be swayed back into a club role, O’Neill would be a great option.

Admittedly, this feels straight out of the Pozzo playbook, but Fabio Grosso could be an intriguing option for Watford to consider. The 48-year-old was relieved of his Fiorentina duties after just four games, but he was a hit at Sassuolo and has a good record in Serie B, having also won promotion with Frosinone.

Grosso took them back to Serie A and they finished 11th in their first season back. He likes his team to play vertically in possession, getting the ball forward quickly, and to be compact defensively.

He’s another motivational figure who can breathe life into the Watford squad. Grosso could be tempted by the chance to manage in England, and his profile in Italy could see them attract some good players outside of the Pozzo ownership.

The fallout from Saints sending employees to watch rivals train saw them kicked out of the play-offs, and they’re still paying the price for that now, with a four-point deduction applied to the current campaign.

However, when Tonda Eckert avoided an immediate touchline ban back in October, it did at least close the case for Saints, and the focus is now entirely on winning promotion this season.

To their credit, Eckert and the players didn’t allow all the off-field noise to distract them, and they carried on the excellent form they had shown under the German last season.

That had put Eckert on the radar of other clubs, with reports claiming that sides in the Premier League and across Europe were monitoring the 33-year-old.

Therefore, Saints have moved to tie down Eckert to a longer contract, and it was announced on Friday that he had signed a deal that runs until 2029.

When you look at how Southampton have been transformed under the boss, it’s fully deserved, as he inherited a team that were struggling towards the bottom of the Championship.

Following on from that, Saints would have been relaxed about interest in Eckert, because the reality is that he was always going to attract attention when you look at their results and performances.

Let's not forget, Southampton didn't just excel in the Championship under Eckert last season, as they beat Arsenal in the FA Cup and pushed Man City all the way in their semi-final clash.

FLW have reeled off some of the second tier's performers who are so easy on the eye

Results will dictate how things play out, but Saints have put things in place for Eckert to lead them to what they will hope is a successful era.

Even though Eckert will appreciate the loyalty Saints have shown to him, he will have his own ambitions as a head coach, and he won’t stick around forever.

#2179. QPR can ease Arsenal transfer fear with major decision that Jimmy Dunne would love

Leon Scarlett is already attracting the attention of some of Europe's biggest clubs as a result of his appearances for the Wales under-21 team, and this puts pressure on his current club to tie him down to a professional contract.

One of the more notable downsides of the information age is that when a football club unearths a rare gem, it won't be very long before the game's apex predators find out about them as well. With every game now recorded and scrutinised, it's seldom long before news of an emerging talent will land with them, and they will be likely to take an interest in the player concerned before they become prohibitively expensive.

In the case of the 17-year-old winger Leon Scarlett, Queens Park Rangers might have a star of the future on their hands. Scarlett has only made six appearances for Rangers, of which five have been as a substitute, and he has yet to record his first goal or assist in a Rangers shirt, but such is his already growing reputation that some big names, including Arsenal, AC Milan and Eintracht Frankfurt have already been connected with an interest in him, among a rapidly growing list of clubs.

In a tight Championship table, Queens Park Rangers have acquitted themselves well in 2026-27 and look capable of battling for promotion this term.

But while Rangers fans can get excited about the possibility of a serious bid for a play-off place or beyond following years of stagnation in the table, it's the attention being lavished upon Leon Scarlett which gives them cause to be the most excited, but in all likelihood also a little nervous over the possibility of losing him.

How far do you think Leon Scarlett could go in his professional career? Let us know in the comments below!

Scarlett, who can play on either the left or the right wing, originally joined QPR's academy following his free transfer arrival from Arsenal in April 2025, and made his debut for them from the bench in their 3-0 loss at Ipswich Town at the very end of the 2025-26 season. So far this season, he's made a further five appearances in a hooped shirt, including a full debut for them against Preston North End in September, although he was withdrawn at half-time in this match.

But QPR aren't the only team for whom he's been playing. Although still only 17-years-old, and having already played for their under-16 and under-17 teams, he made two brief appearances for the Wales under-21 team against Belgium and Austria at the end of September, while he also completed three appearances for the under-19 team during the November international break which included providing an assist in their 2-2 draw with Iceland in a play-off match for the Under-19 Euros which they won on penalty kicks.

These tastes of international football have grown the young winger's profile. At the end of last week, Anthony Joseph of Sky Sports reported that both AC Milan and Eintracht Frankfurt are keeping tabs on him, while it's also been reported that Brighton, Rangers and even his former club Arsenal could be plotting a move for him. And the pressure on Rangers over Scarlett could be all the greater for knowing that the winger hasn't yet signed his first full professional contract with the Loftus Road club.

QPR prodigy Leon Scarlett is attracting interest from the likes of AC Milan and Eintracht Frankfurt, according to new reports...

Both the Queens Park Rangers club captain Jimmy Dunne and manager Julien Stephan are clear admirers of Leon Scarlett. As reported by Loft For Words in September, Dunne spoke about the teenager at a fans forum in glowing terms, saying: "Just watching Leon Scarlett today he’s so impressive, so bright, and so positive. You want to see him do well and thrive. We’ve got loads of exciting players like that. I was here at the U21 game the other day and they were fabulous."

Julien Stephan also praised him at this forum, saying: "Why in the last two games did I pick Leon Scarlett? Because he deserves it. He showed in all the training sessions it was the right moment for him. Never a coincidence. Always logical."

In April, as reported by the Evening Standard, Stephan had previously said of Scarlett: "The last game (Scarlett) did for the U21s, he did very well. I saw him in a cup game with the U18s earlier in the season, and he did a good first half. So I just wanted to see him during the session with us (the first team). And during the session, he did well.” Scarlett earned his senior debut shortly after this.

There is one thing that Queens Park Rangers can do to try and secure their position regarding this young talent. Scarlett remains on a scholarship with the club and hasn't yet signed his first full professional contract with them. Rangers should surely try to tie him down to a senior contract, which would mean that, in the event that he continues to show the promise that he has so far and clubs remain interested in snatching him from them, they would be able to land a substantial transfer fee for him.

This could, of course, end in disappointment. Scarlett has the right to say no to any offer made to him, and any refusal to agree terms with Rangers would surely be a precursor to him leaving the club. But as things stand, the club would have next to no chance of keeping hold of him, and with the list of clubs who are tracking him continuing to grow, Queens Park Rangers might be best advised to do everything within their power to keep this exciting young prospect at their club for as long as possible. Judging by his comments in September, it would certainly make Jimmy Dunne happy.

#2178. Jordan James made a decision few players would consider before joining Wolves

Wolves had an eventful summer after their embarrassing relegation from the Premier League last season, with Jordan James among the arrivals.

Many expected a huge turnover of players at Molineux, but whilst that didn’t happen, there was a refresh of the group, and Cesar Peixoto’s squad was boosted by some high-profile additions.

Bringing in Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez on free transfers caught the eye, and James was another arrival that was seen as a coup, as he was named Young Player of the Year in the Championship following his performances at Leicester last season.

Despite the Foxes’ struggles, James was outstanding, scoring 11 goals in 34 games for a side that were relegated to League One.

Wolves are mounting their challenge for an immediate return to Premier League football and sit 3rd in the Championship table. Their talented squad are in impressive form, but Cesar Peixoto and co will have eyes on potential reinforcements ahead of the January transfer window.

According to Sky Sports, among the players on Wanderers’ radar is Liel Abada. The 25-year-old winger sees his contract at Charlotte FC expire in December, and his impending free agent status means he is being tracked by a number of Championship clubs.

Abada would be strong competition for the likes of Rafiki Said, Mateus Mane and Rodrigo Gomes. He can join for nothing and further strengthen Peixoto’s frontline, and at 25, he has the time and room to grow into a potential Premier League player for the Old Gold.

#2176. Romelu Lukaku announces 'bombshell' international retirement: Former Chelsea star, 33, U-turns on his Belgium future - leaving Belgian press stunned

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 08:03 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:49 EST, 16 November 2026

Romelu Lukaku has announced his retirement from international football in a 'bombshell' decision that has left the Belgian press utterly stunned.

The former Chelsea and Manchester United forward, 33, vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament with the Belgium national team, although he now appears to have changed his mind over his future.

Describing his international career as a 'great ride', Lukaku took to social media on Monday morning to break the unexpected news.

'16 years old,' his Instagram statement began. 'For 16 years, I gave everything for the national team. I experienced every possible emotion. I played with fantastic teammates for whom I will always be grateful.

'I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches for pushing me and giving me the confidence to help the team. It was a great ride, and I enjoyed every moment.

'To the Belgian fans, thank you for the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at four World Cups and three European Championships. I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing, it was a joy. I am grateful. Thank you.'

Belgium legend Romelu Lukaku has announced his decision to retire from international football

Lukaku vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament

The Belgian forward has fallen down the pecking order and spent a lot of time on the bench

The Belgian veteran accompanied his post with a gallery of photographs from his storied international career, from his debut against Croatia under Dick Advocaat in 2010 to his final chapter wearing the armband.

Lukaku has captained Belgium on a handful of occasions since 2020, alongside the likes of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans.

The 33-year-old forward, who became one of the hottest properties in world football after breaking on the scene at Chelsea, has been a regular fixture in the international set-up for almost two decades.

Spearheading Belgium's golden generation, which included star-studded talents such as De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, Lukaku chalked up an impressive 135 caps for the international team.

He also retires as Belgium's all-time top scorer on 94 goals, just six shy of a century.

Belgian newspapers were caught out by the shock announcement, which was described as an 'unexpected bombshell' by outlet HLN on Monday.

Lukaku's stock within the international set-up has fallen since he promised the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament in January.

After suffering multiple injury setbacks, he featured at the tournament under Rudi Garcia and continued to play a crucial role, scoring three times as a substitute to guide Belgium to the quarter-finals where they were ultimately stopped by eventual champions Spain.

Since Mark van Bommel's appointment in August, following Garcia's departure at the end of his contract, Lukaku has slipped further down the pecking order, with Charles De Ketelaere preferred to lead the line.

Lukaku, pictured with Kevin De Bruyne, was an unused substitute as Belgium beat Italy 4-1

During Belgium's resounding 4-1 victory over Italy on Sunday, Lukaku warmed the bench as an unused substitute - and wasn't even in the squad to face Turkey three days before.

While Belgium were winning in the second half against the Italians, Lukaku was seen warming up on the sidelines in the hope of featuring for one last time, but unfortunately was not given the opportunity.

VTM NIEUWS anchor Maarten Breckx claimed De Bruyne looked 'concerned' while speaking to Lukaku on the bench, suggesting the former Man City star was unhappy to see his team-mate overlooked.

'When it became clear that he wouldn't be allowed to come on, De Bruyne was talking to him. You could see the concern in his eyes,' he said.

'You could tell, especially from Romelu's attitude, that he was dissatisfied and displeased. He had probably counted on getting some minutes...'

With only Jan Vertonghen and Axel Witsel registering more international caps than Lukaku over their careers, boasting 157 and 140 appearances respectively, Belgium are expected to give the 33-year-old forward a send-off he deserves in the near future.

Witsel, who also called time on his Belgium career this year, was one of the team-mates to celebrate Lukaku's retirement on Instagram.

'Thanks for everything, legend. Thank you, what a journey we've had together,' he wrote.

#2174. The 8-figure sum it will cost to buy Bradford City as overseas takeover interest grows

Bradford City are up for sale, but the price put on the club by owner Stefan Rupp could be off-putting to those seeking to buy into the West Yorkshire club.

Bradford City marked their return to League action following the international break with a 2-2 home draw against Doncaster Rovers. A Sean Grehan goal for Doncaster salvaged the visitors a point, but the draw was still enough to lift the Bantams back into the play-off places as a result of Plymouth Argyle's surprise 2-0 home defeat to Peterborough United.

But while Bradford's current position remains encouraging, there has been a degree of uncertainty surrounding the future of the club amid reports that owners Stefan Rupp and Edin Radic could be planning to sell up and move on.

The club are reportedly of interest to a Thai consortium who are looking to buy a club and who have had an interest in EFL clubs in the past.

Reporting on his Patreon on Sunday morning, journalist Alan Nixon has reported that the asking price for Bradford City is £11 million, though he adds that this price doesn't include the club's Valley Parade home itself, which has been owned by the pension fund of former chairman Gordon Gibb since 2004.

Nixon confirms that "there is interest in the Yorkshire club and they could potentially be sold", but adds that "the owners are looking for an eight-digit sum and that seems high when they do not own the ground".

Would you support new ownership at Bradford City, or would you rather stick with the current group? Let us know in the comments below!

However, he does add that this doesn't necessarily mean the end of interest in buying them, saying that, "potential buyers have been in contact with Gordon Gibb, the Valley Parade landlord, and could go in with him".

Although Gibb hasn't been directly involved in the running of Bradford City in over two decades, he is a key player in any sale of the club, despite being based in Scarborough and being a Leeds United fan - the Whites are West Yorkshire rivals of the Bantams, but of course they are two divisions apart.

Bradford City are reportedly being targeted in a takeover bid from a Thai-based group, who are keen on taking over the club from Stefan Rupp.

Selling a club in the bottom two divisions of the EFL which doesn't own its own ground is very different to selling a club which does. Since the other assets that the club owns aren't usually especially valuable, the ground itself is often by far the biggest and most valuable that the club owns.

Those who buy a club which doesn't own its own home are usually buying little more than the contracts, the right to play in the EFL, and the name of the club itself. Many prospective owners will want to 'reunite' the club with its ground when they purchase it, as happened with Coventry City last year, where owner Doug King managed to secure the purchase of The CBS Arena, almost three years after buying the club itself.

Bradford reportedly pay more than £500,000 annually to lease the ground, with the existing agreement due for renewal in 2028, and that amount of money as an ongoing cost limits what the club can spend elsewhere. But Gibb is under no obligation to sell, and it's not known what he would want for it.

The last set of company accounts for the club confirmed that a "net loss of (£996,814) in 2024 has been augmented by a further loss in the current year of (£2,992,958)", so Bradford City are not currently profitable, and any new owners would be aware that profitability might only come should they manage to get the club all the way up to the Premier League.

But Bradford City have been moving in an upward direction over the last two or three years following years of stagnation in League Two, and the size of the club, who can still attract attendances of close to 20,000 and represent a city of half a million people, will be appealing to investors looking for a project that they can grow. But the cost of the stadium itself is a clear complication in the sale of the club, and it might mean that negotiations take some time to conclude.

#2172. Klopp breaks ranks to savage Infantino: Liverpool legend becomes first boss to turn on FIFA president - who is WORSE than Sepp Blatter - as pressure mounts after World Cup farce

Published: 08:02 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 10:36 EST, 16 November 2026

Jurgen Klopp has called on FIFA's embattled president Gianni Infantino to resign, becoming the first national team manager to do so.

Infantino's reputation took a nosedive after his sycophantic behaviour towards Donald Trump before and during the World Cup - most memorably by awarding him a 'FIFA Peace Prize'.

And it only got worse when his clandestine plot to sell off stakes in the World Cup, a devious scheme which would have banked him millions, was revealed by The Times.

Now Germany manager Klopp has hit out: 'There is now a unanimous consensus that a change would make sense.

'I thought that, after Sepp Blatter, the situation couldn't get any worse - but here we are.

'Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job.

Jurgen Klopp has publicly savaged FIFA president Gianni Infantino, becoming the first national team manager to do so

The Germany manager said Infantino - who tried to sell off stakes in the World Cup to his own benefit - is 'worse' than his predecessor Sepp Blatter

'Without a doubt, there are people who truly care about football and have no financial interests,' the former Liverpool manager said.

Infantino has clung on to his job thus far, surviving a crisis summit in Morocco in August, despite intense and widespread opposition.

A total of 90 nations including all of UEFA's teams rebelled, with threats to boycott FIFA competitions, and Infantino's £3.1billion plan fell apart.

But he still maintained a large swell of support among Africa, Asia, and South America - especially after offering each nation £30million if they supported his plan. His opponents pointed out that he could simply have given money from FIFA's cash reserves of roughly £4.5b.

In the pages of this historic newspaper, football legend Luis Figo wrote that 'Infantino must go' and accused him of 'debasing the office of FIFA President'.

FIFA does not have a history of picking good leaders - Blatter resigned in 2015 amid allegations of corruption, though he was cleared alongside Michel Platini last year.

Infantino now looks well-placed to be re-elected for a fourth term in next March's presidential elections.

The deadline for candidacies to be submitted is November 18.

Philippe Diallo, the French Football Federation president, has agreed to run against Infantino and has the backing of UEFA's executive committee.

'(Diallo has) extensive experience across all levels of the game, having led the organisation representing French professional football clubs, served on the board of the French professional league and within FIFA’s dispute resolution structures, before becoming President of the FFF and a member of the UEFA Executive Committee in 2023,' UEFA said.

Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega has already announced his intention to be a rival to Infantino.

Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japanese Football Association, is also reportedly set to mount a challenge.

Ex-Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger was touted as a potential challenger but it is understood he told European football’s governing body UEFA that he would not stand.

#2169. Is Mauricio Pochettino’s job at Manchester United the toughest in the Premier League?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United hired Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager to replace Michael Carrick, who managed just one win in 10 games.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

Pochettino brings considerable Premier League experience after previous spells with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. He has also managed Paris Saint-Germain before the USA job.

As he faces Liverpool for his first game on Sunday, the question arises: is he facing the toughest job in the Premier League?

The question was posed on BBC Radio about who is going to have more pressure, Pochettino or Thomas Frank at Crystal Palace.

According to former Premier League defender Nedum Onuoha, the expectations surrounding Manchester United will make the Argentine’s job considerably harder.

Pochettino is preparing for his first game in charge of Manchester United, with Liverpool waiting at Anfield on November 22. However, the challenge facing the new manager goes beyond getting results on the pitch.

Onuoha believes Pochettino will have to deal with constant discussion and criticism about his work, much of it coming from former United players who are now in the media.

Choosing between Pochettino and Frank, Onuoha said, “Probably Pochettino, because every former Manchester United player works in the media, so there will always be discussion around what he is doing.

“Whereas Frank can just enjoy playing his football at Crystal Palace. If he does well then it is great, if he doesn’t do well then it is still OK.

“But from Pochettino’s perspective, if Manchester United finish the season 15th in the Premier League, whether we like it or not, there will be some criticism of him because he’s had 28 games to do something.”

The comments just highlight the difference in expectations at the two clubs. Frank may have more freedom to work without the same level of attention, while Pochettino will be judged from day one against the standards historically associated with Manchester United. That is one big problem for Pochettino.

Rory Smith from The Observer highlighted another glaring problem at United.  Highlighting a major problem, Smith said, “there is a cycle element to Manchester United whereby a manager comes in, makes things a bit better, and then within a year to 18 months they aren’t challenging for titles again because the Premier League has changed since they were a dominant force.”

Pochettino’s first taste of action as a United manager will be against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22. That opening fixture will give him an immediate test, but the bigger task will be to get back United to winning ways, step by step.

Will the Manchester United job be without pressure for Mauricio Pochettino? Absolutely Not.

Julien Stephan's side currently occupy the final position in the revamped play-offs and are playing some of the best football in the second tier, per the underlying numbers. They have the fourth-best xG difference in the league, and only Middlesbrough and Wolves have a better xGA.

A lot of the players who QPR signed in the past few seasons, either from League One or as youngsters from Premier League clubs and abroad, are starting to blossom into very good top-end Championship players, and it's being reflected in their results.

There's apt depth everywhere in the squad, perhaps other than in central midfield. Ball-playing centre-back Ronnie Edwards, who has played in the engine room before at Peterborough United, has been called in to deputise at times, either due to Nicolas Madsen's injury or a lack of form for Jonathan Varane.

Glen Kamara was QPR's marquee midfield signing this past summer, with the former play-off finalist at Leeds United joining on loan to form an engine room core with Madsen and Varane.

However, the Hoops' unlucky history with injuries in recent times caught up with Madsen, who should be back shortly. But it did leave Julien Stephan light in those areas and, as mentioned, Edwards was called in to deputise as Kamara worked his way into the side, coming in instead of Varane.

Therefore, FLW's QPR fan pundit, Louis Moir, wants to see his side bolster their midfield options in case injury strikes again, and would like to see Fulham's Harrison Reed arrive on loan.

"One player I'd like to see join, and I'm not sure it's even that ambitious, is Harrison Reed. I've always liked him as a player across the years; he's really tidy, neat, does the hard work and has shown his ability in the Premier League," he said.

"I think with this season, Madsen has been out a bit, Kamara has obviously come in and has been class, but Varane hasn't been at his best, so we're kind of lacking in midfield.

"You never want a serious injury to occur to someone like Kamara, for example, and Edwards has come in and done a great job in midfield, but I just feel we could do with one more, and that's mainly due to Varane not being at his best. I think it [the midfield] can be a weak point if Madsen or Kamara are out."

Varane was one of QPR's best performers pre-Stephan, to the point where the Hoops were reportedly rejecting £4 million offers from La Liga side Espanyol for his services. There is a player there, but that hasn't been seen this season, especially. With Reed in the squad, the R's could maintain this early-season play-off form if injuries do continue to haunt them.

Reed is well-respected at Fulham and has been a great servant to the club in the seven years he's been playing at Craven Cottage. However, the club is starting to outgrow the 31-year-old.

He made just seven league appearances last season, remaining unused from the bench on 22 separate occasions. Funnily enough, one of those cameo bench appearances saw him score the Premier League's Goal of the Season in a 2-2 draw with Liverpool in January.

This season, under Alvaro Arbeloa, Reed's role in the squad has decreased even further. Now, the midfielder isn't getting into matchday squads in the Premier League, and all his appearances so far have been in the EFL Cup.

Do you think Harrison Reed will be a primary loan target for Championship sides this summer? Let us know in the comments.

"I think Reed may be of interest to a few Championship clubs," says Moir, due to his standing in the Fulham fold. "But him on loan would be more than ideal and a really top signing.

"I think it's more than realistic, more than ambitious, and would fit in really well. He'd add a lot of bite to the midfield and more depth. You wouldn't have to worry about him starting each week, but he'd come on and do a good job."

Reed's long-term future at Fulham is up in the air. The 31-year-old's four-year deal, which he signed back in 2023, is up at the end of the campaign.

There is an option for the Cottagers to extend that by a year, but the likelihood of that happening seems quite slim, especially if Arbeloa's side remain in the Premier League this season.

So, Reed could be in a situation where a loan move in January could almost be a way for a loaning team to have a six-month trial before a decision is made about handing him a longer-term contract.

Ranking the Championship clubs based on how successful they've been since the start of 2001/02

If QPR remain a Championship side, this could definitely be a decision that they make. Reed has 131 Premier League appearances and has won promotion from the Championship twice with Fulham. At 32, he could be the perfect veteran option in the middle for a side that were on the cusp of promotion and want to go again in 2027/28.

Obviously, the Hoops will want to go up this year, and Reed could help aid in that, too, but thinking longer term, getting the 31-year-old through the door could be quite an underrated move for this R's side.
