#2145. Manu Koné: Roma slap £86m price tag on Chelsea target

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Roma have put an £86m (€100m) price tag on Manu Koné, according to Gazzetta dello Sport, reviving the Manu Koné Chelsea transfer link that first emerged over the summer. Roma want any interested club, including Chelsea, to know the price before serious talks can even begin.

Koné remains under contract at the Stadio Olimpico, and he has become a key part of Roma’s midfield since his move from Borussia Mönchengladbach. The Gazzetta report reads like a warning to potential buyers rather than proof of any talks between the two clubs.

Roma sporting director Tony D’Amico has confirmed Chelsea made contact late in the summer window, though he was quick to draw a clear line under how far things went.

“There was an inquiry and some preliminary contact with Chelsea on the final day of the transfer window. No official offers arrived that would allow us to approach the player. Something was imagined that simply didn’t happen. There was no official offer; the final day of the transfer window got everyone a little worked up.”

D’Amico’s comments confirm Chelsea looked at signing Koné before the deadline, but they stop well short of showing an official bid was ever made. He also explained why Roma had no wish to sell a key player so close to the window closing.

“Before the match against Fiorentina (on 24 August), I said it would be difficult for us to deprive ourselves of important players so near to the end of the transfer session, and so it proved. Kone is an important player, we’re happy he stayed with us, and we’re confident he’ll give his contribution during the season.”

Chelsea’s midfield has changed shape under Xabi Alonso since the summer, with Morgan Rogers arriving to add depth and competition for places. That signing came during a window that also saw exits acceleration under Xabi Alonso, as the head coach reshaped his squad around his own style.

Koné’s ball winning and his range of progressive passing would suit Alonso well, should Chelsea ever revisit their interest. Supporters have already seen how Alonso rotates his midfield for the biggest games, including the recent derby line-up selections against Brentford.

For now, Rogers and Chelsea’s existing central options give Alonso enough cover without needing an immediate signing. Roma’s reluctance to sell also means any deal would need patience rather than a quick resolution.

Nothing in D’Amico’s comments suggests Roma are open to a sale in the near term, and Koné has given no sign that he wants to leave. The £86m valuation, reported by Football London, stands as Roma’s marker rather than an asking price involved with Chelsea.

Will Chelsea return with a more formal approach in a future window? D’Amico’s comments give no hint either way. The Manu Koné Chelsea transfer link is unlikely to fade given Chelsea’s history of scouting France’s leading midfielders, but any fresh move will have to wait for Roma’s stance to soften.

#2144. New footage shows what Ryan Manning did during Southampton's 2nd goal v Derby County

Southampton strolled to a comfortable 2-0 victory over Derby County at the weekend, but what Ryan Manning did in the build-up to the second goal ought to have Saints fans laughing.

Southampton have continued to climb the Championship table with their latest 2-0 home victory over struggling Derby at St Mary's on Saturday, courtesy of goals from Cyle Larin and Divin Mubama.

Despite Derby's insistence on disrupting Southampton's flow, the home side dominated large parts of the game and were deserving of the three points in the end, as Irish left-back Manning has certainly had the last laugh.

Football League World has asked AI to predict the 2027/28 EFL Championship table if Manchester United and Manchester City were in it

It took Southampton a while to really get going in their clash against Derby, with just one shot on target from either side in the first half, making it an extremely close encounter.

However, Eckert's half-time team talk appeared to have the effect the German would've been hoping for, as the Saints broke the deadlock with Larin just before the hour mark, before finally adding a second in the dying embers as Mubama raced through on goal to prod into an empty net following a Derby corner.

With Rams goalkeeper Jacob Widell Zetterström trying his luck in the penalty area in the closing stages, Mubama broke away after Lewis Dobbin played him through on goal, and running alongside the Manchester City loanee was Manning, who turned and appeared to laugh at the chasing Derby defenders.

The 30-year-old, who has developed into one of the best left-backs on the South Coast, has certainly endeared himself to the Southampton supporters since his arrival at the club in 2023, with this just being a fresh reminder of his character and importance to the side.

Manning's contract at St Mary's is due to expire in the summer, and as things stand, he's set to leave as a free agent in 2027.

However, he has made his intentions of staying at the club abundantly clear already, and having become a mainstay under Eckert, it would be a surprise if he wasn't offered fresh terms on the South Coast, regardless of whether a return to the Premier League is secured.

The Irishman will be free to speak to other clubs over a summer move in January, and with just over a month until the winter window, Southampton shouldn't leave this issue unresolved for much longer.

What have you made of Ryan Manning's time at Southampton? Would you like to see him offered a fresh deal? Share your thoughts below!

With Southampton climbing into the Championship play-off picture, Eckert will have set his sights firmly on the automatic promotion places right now.

If it weren't for their four-point deduction at the beginning of the campaign, the Saints would currently sit in 3rd place behind only Middlesbrough and Stoke City, level on points with Wolverhampton Wanderers but with a superior goal difference.

#2143. Liverpool vs Man Utd: Preview, key stats, team news & where to watch

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Mauricio Pochettino begins his Manchester United reign with a huge test at Anfield on Sunday, with Manchester United desperate for a result after making their worst start to a top-flight season in 40 years.

Manchester United have collected just eight points from their opening 10 Premier League matches, with one win and five draws leaving them 18th in the table. They have also conceded in every league game this season and are currently on a run of 11 consecutive matches without keeping a clean sheet in all competitions.

Mauricio Pochettino only arrived to the club on Wednesday after replacing Michael Carrick, leaving him with just a few training sessions to prepare for one of the biggest fixtures in English football.

There is some encouragement for the Argentine, however. Eight of United’s last nine permanent or caretaker managers have avoided defeat in their first match in charge. That may be some encouragement to the Argentine.

Meanwhile, Liverpool are not exactly enjoying a comfortable season at home either. They sit fourth with 18 points but have won just once in their five Premier League matches at Anfield so far, giving them the third-worst home record in the Premier League.

Their recent form across all competitions stands at three wins, one draw and two defeats in their last six matches. Liverpool most recently beat Crystal Palace 3-1, but they will know that United’s poor league position does not make this fixture any less complicated.

Liverpool have received positive news ahead of Sunday’s meeting. Dominik Szoboszlai and Virgil van Dijk are both expected to feature, while Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong could also be available.

Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni have returned to team training following knee injuries but are unlikely to make the squad. Hugo Ekitike remains a long-term absentee with an Achilles problem.

Manchester United could welcome back Patrick Dorgu and Harry Maguire after both trained following fitness concerns. They were seen in that leaked drone footage as well. Lisandro Martínez is also available again after serving his suspension.

Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford could return, although their availability remains uncertain. Carlos Baleba, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko are still sidelined.

The new United boss has a difficult personal record against Liverpool. Pochettino has faced the Reds 19 times, winning three, drawing five and losing 11. He has also failed to win any of his last eight meetings with them in all competitions. That might be a concern, but everything has a first time.

Pochettino will be encouraged by United’s overall record against Liverpool.  United have an edge with 85 wins compared to Liverpool’s 72 across 218 meetings. Their most recent encounter also went their way, with a 3-2 victory on May 3.

However, United arrive on a disappointing run of seven consecutive away matches without a win and have managed just one victory in their last 11 games.

A Rangers season-ticket holder and freelance writer, he has previously written for Vital Rangers, Rangers Review, Football Ground Guide and Give Me Sport, and has a long association with the Follow Follow fanzine.

Joao Pedro missed Chelsea’s 3-0 Premier League defeat to Brentford with a knee problem, and the injury has since ruled him out of Brazil’s squad for the friendlies against Australia and India.

He was absent from Xabi Alonso’s confirmed lineups against Brentford, with Chelsea turning to other forward options instead.

Brazil’s coaching staff confirmed the withdrawal, pointing to the same knee issue that kept him out of the derby. Chelsea have not set a firm return date for Joao Pedro, leaving supporters to wait for further updates during the international break.

The Joao Pedro injury situation took a new turn when the Standard reported that he is seeing a specialist during the international break to speed up his recovery.

According to the Standard, the forward is using this pause in the calendar to get ahead of the problem rather than wait for Chelsea to resume domestic action.

Chelsea have not issued their own statement on the specialist visit, and the club’s official line on Joao Pedro’s fitness remains limited to his withdrawal from matchday duty.

Full detail on the reported treatment can be found in football.london’s reported injury update, which first carried the specialist claim alongside Xabi Alonso’s comments on the striker’s season.

Until Chelsea confirm otherwise, the Standard’s report stands as the clearest picture of how the club are handling the knee concern.

It suggests a measured approach, with recovery prioritised over rushing Joao Pedro back into contention for the next fixture.

Before the injury forced him out, Xabi Alonso had made his admiration for Joao Pedro clear. The Chelsea manager ranked the forward among the Premier League’s elite strikers, alongside Manchester City’s Erling Haaland.

“If you count how many top strikers we have in the Premier League, I’m sure that João is there, Haaland for sure is there.

“So I would rate him that way. He has a very strong goal this year: to have a great season, to score many goals, and to be a nominee for not just this month but more months. I am not surprised, but really happy with the kind of player that we have here with João.”

With Joao Pedro sidelined, Alonso must lean again on the depth built into his squad.

His approach to rotation, part of the squad management this season, faces another test while his in-form forward is unavailable.

#2141. Why can Mauricio Pochettino turn things around at Manchester United?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of his first United game against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, with plenty of questions surrounding the players who will benefit from his arrival.

Manchester United have struggled badly this season, sitting 18th in the Premier League after collecting just eight points from their opening 10 matches.

Pochettino replaces Michael Carrick and his job has been described as one of the toughest jobs in the Premier League. Former defender Wes Brown believes Manchester United have a chance with Pochettino to change things despite it being very difficult.

Brown believes the new manager has enough quality at his disposal to improve the situation, despite the difficult start and the pressure that comes with the Manchester United job.

Asked whether Pochettino faces an impossible task after previous managers failed to bring success to Old Trafford, Brown was confident the Argentine could make a difference.

“Definitely not impossible. Regardless of what has happened so far this season, Manchester United do have good players,” Wes Brown said while talking to Flashscore.

Brown expects Pochettino to demand more effort from the squad.

“He looks like a personable manager, so can work with these players individually to get their confidence up and really play for the shirt and create that positive vibe that seems to be missing.”

Asked about how long Manchester United will take to be a title challenger again, Wes Brown was cautious in putting any numbers.

“Well, it isn’t going to happen overnight. You will need a reaction quickly, that is for sure. They are very far away, but you have to start with consistency and that is something Pochettino has to install and deliver a consistency of play, to be fitter than your opponent and show fight.”

The former defender also highlighted Bruno Fernandes’ drop in form, suggesting the captain could benefit from a change in management.

“You have to see Bruno’s form has dropped, so it will be great to see this pick up under the new manager.”

Pochettino’s priority will be getting a response on Sunday against Liverpool from his senior players. United have been in this cycle of repeating managers and not finding much success. Mauricio Pochettino needs to take things one at a time. Sunday would be that first step.

#2140. Pep Guardiola Speaks Out as Man City Found Guilty of 114 Charges

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 financial charges, the Premier League has confirmed. The verdict follows an eight-week hearing that opened almost two years ago. It closes one of the most significant disciplinary cases in the competition’s history.

Former head coach Pep Guardiola has already broken his silence. Reaction to the Pep Guardiola Man City charges verdict is spreading fast across the division, with Chelsea among the clubs watching closely.

Guardiola joined Manchester City in 2016 and turned them into the dominant force in English football. He left his post earlier this summer, with the club having already worked through plans to replace Pep Guardiola at City.

His exit means he holds no formal role at the Etihad. Yet he moved quickly to make his loyalty clear once the ruling landed. According to the football.london report that first carried his statement, Guardiola posted directly to his supporters.

“I want every single @ManCity fan to know I am here; more than ever. I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman [Khaldoon Al Mubarak], Ferran [Soriano], the players, staff, Enzo [Maresca] and you, our unique supporters. Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all.”

Manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano has confirmed that the club intends to appeal the verdict. The statement from Guardiola comes to City’s defence despite him leaving the role this summer. He is still viewed as the man who built this era of success, even though he no longer sits in the dugout at the Etihad.

The Pep Guardiola Man City charges case matters just as much to Chelsea as it does to Manchester City themselves. Chelsea, along with Arsenal and Tottenham, are among the Premier League clubs directly affected by the outcome. Every point City may have gained through breaches has a knock on effect further down the table.

Most top flight clubs including Chelsea are now pushing for City to face relegation as a consequence of the verdict. Some are reported to be weighing up legal action of their own. Guardiola has spoken about Chelsea before, including Guardiola’s previous comments on Chelsea. This latest statement fits a pattern of public backing for Manchester City, despite the criticism now directed at the club.

For Chelsea supporters, the case is not just about points on a table. It touches on the integrity of seasons they competed in directly. That is why so many rivals are refusing to let the matter rest with a guilty verdict alone.

Manchester City’s appeal process is now the next stage in a case that has already run for nearly two years. Ferran Soriano has made clear the club will contest the findings. No date has been confirmed for when that appeal will be heard.

Until then, no points deductions, penalties or changes to past titles have been confirmed by the Premier League. Chelsea and their rivals will be watching the appeal timeline just as closely as they watched the original hearing. The final outcome could still be a long way off.

#2139. Manchester United managerial costs near £100m as Pochettino fee revealed

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Manchester United have spent approximately £95m appointing and dismissing managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013, according to BBC Sport, with the total expected to pass £100m following Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival.

United’s latest financial disclosures confirm a fee of £7.584m in connection with appointing Pochettino, who left his role as United States national team head coach earlier this month.

The figure takes the cumulative cost of managerial changes to around £95m, according to BBC Sport’s analysis. That total is expected to rise once the costs of Michael Carrick’s dismissal and appointing Pochettino’s coaching staff are included.

Pochettino signed a two-and-a-half-year contract on 13 November, replacing Carrick after a difficult start to the Premier League season. The club’s Stock Market filing states that the appointment fee will be recognised in its financial accounts for the current quarter. United also confirmed borrowing a further £10m on 16 November, taking the amount drawn on their revolving credit facility to £240m.

Pochettino is United’s ninth full-time managerial appointment since Ferguson’s departure, including Ralf Rangnick’s interim spell. The club have also changed managers during each of the past three seasons.

United’s financial disclosures show that their long-term debt stood at £577.4m on 30 September, while outstanding transfer-fee commitments totalled £417m. Those figures are separate from the cost of appointing and dismissing managers.

A Reuters analysis has put the wider cost of managerial and senior football staff changes above £100m, using a broader calculation. Pochettino now faces the task of improving United’s results, beginning with Sunday’s Premier League trip to Liverpool.

Bournemouth will block any Alex Scott Chelsea transfer in January. That is according to reports from the Daily Mail and BBC Sport. Both outlets say the Cherries want to keep their young midfielder as they fight to protect their Premier League status this season.

Chelsea have been linked with serious interest in the 22-year-old. Reports suggest the Blues have already tested Bournemouth’s resolve with a bid worth close to £64 million. Bournemouth have given no indication they are willing to negotiate. Scott, the reports say, simply is not for sale this winter.

Reports in the Daily Mail and on BBC Sport state that Bournemouth have no intention of sanctioning a sale this winter. The club’s hierarchy reportedly view Scott as central to their survival plan, wary of leaning on new signings mid-season rather than trusting the squad they already have.

A fee of around £64 million, first reported by Football London, is said to have been offered by Chelsea during recent discussions.

Scott joined Bournemouth from Bristol City in 2023. He has quickly become one of the most sought-after young midfielders in English football. Interest from a club the size of Chelsea shows how far his reputation has grown, though Bournemouth’s stance makes a January move increasingly unlikely.

Scott’s rise has been underlined by his first appearance for England. He came off the bench for a 20-minute cameo as Thomas Tuchel’s side beat Czechia 2-0 in the Nations League. The manager praised him afterwards.

“Alex Scott has maybe one of the best performances in midfield in the Premier League since the start with Bournemouth.”

“Individually he’s one of the outstanding midfielders so he clearly deserves to be with us.”

“He took another step into the right direction. Very impressive and happy that he is on that route. Now he plays in Europe for Bournemouth and deserves to be with us.”

That praise from their former manager will only increase Chelsea’s interest. Scott’s energy and composure suit the identity Xabi Alonso wants to build at Stamford Bridge. The Spaniard has already shown he is willing to rotate his squad, as seen in Xabi Alonso’s squad management decisions this season.

Chelsea travel to face Bournemouth in the Premier League soon. It is a fixture that will give Alonso a close look at a player repeatedly linked with his club. Build-up to that game is already underway, with team news arriving ahead of the Bournemouth clash.

The prospects of an Alex Scott Chelsea transfer happening in January now look slim. Supporters hoping for fresh competition in central midfield may need patience, with Chelsea more likely to revisit their interest when the summer window opens.

#2137. Arsenal Women vs Barcelona: Arsenal show their resilience with impressive draw against Barcelona

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal Women vs Barcelona: Arsenal Women claimed a vital point at the Camp Nou. They drew 1-1 against Barcelona in the Champions League on Thursday night.

Frida Maanum gave the Gunners the lead in the first half. Caroline Graham Hansen scored to bring the game level after the break. Whilst Renee Slegers will be disappointed to miss out on all three points, her side played some encouraging football.

Despite needing to play differently, Arsenal had an even game against an opposition who would inevitably have long periods of the ball. The visitors played very well defensively and looked dangerous when they could attack.

The result showed that Slegers has a team that can adapt to new challenges. This could be important for Arsenal as they try to make a mark in Europe.

One of the key decisions made by Slegers was to include Maanum. She had only recently returned from injury but made an impressive impact against Barcelona.

The midfielder scored early on to start the game in the right direction. Slegers was very impressed with her play when not in possession. She was praised for her communication skills and assisting others.

Arsenal’s attacking play was mainly based on fast counter attacks. They knew they wouldn’t be able to play in the same style as Barcelona and therefore tried to take advantage of the space on offer.

However, there were chances created in both halves. Arsenal may have been more clinical with their chances, they were always a threat.

Eventually, Barcelona scored their equaliser through Graham Hansen. Slegers said that Arsenal lost their shape during the move, which gave Hansen too much space.

It was a reminder of how quickly Barcelona can strike if you lose your concentration for a moment.

The Arsenal manager was pleased with the way her players implemented the game plan, showing tenacity, discipline, good communication and bravery.

Slegers admitted Arsenal did lose the ball too much in the second half, and by keeping it longer, they would have taken the pressure off defending against Barca’s dangerous attack.

There was some frustration that Arsenal couldn’t hold onto their lead, and there were more chances created towards the end of the game. The visitors got into good positions to win corners but couldn’t get the winning goal.

They will feel very positive from their display. They put themselves up against one of the biggest tests in the Camp Nou and proved that they can cause Barcelona problems.

There isn’t much time to really reflect on the result ahead of their game against the London City Lionesses on Sunday, but Slegers now has another example of what her side can do when they play with purpose and structure.

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Bruno Fernandes has been Manchester United’s most creative player since his arrival to the club in 2020.

The 32-year-old is approaching the final months of his current deal, which expires at the end of the season. United do have the option to extend his contract by another 12 months, keeping him at Old Trafford until 2028.

While they can extend his contract for a year, Manchester United are actively pursuing a deal to tie Bruno Fernandes beyond 2028.

Bruno Fernandes himself has now confirmed that the club have offered him a new contract, but the midfielder has made it clear that he does not want discussions about his future to become a priority right now.

Fernandes confirmed that an offer had been made but dismissed suggestions that he was holding out for a better salary or a longer agreement.

“The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay,” he told Sky Sports.

He also insisted that money has never been the reason behind his decision to remain at United, despite having opportunities to move elsewhere in previous transfer windows.

“If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here,” Fernandes said.

The Portugal international added that he could have earned considerably more by accepting offers from other clubs, but always chose to continue his career in Manchester.

Fernandes revealed that discussions initially took place towards the end of last season and continued when the players returned for pre-season.

However, the United captain believes the current situation at the club makes it the wrong time to focus on his personal future.

“We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side,” he explained.

“I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.”

Fernandes has been one of United’s most influential players since arriving from Sporting in 2020. He has scored 75 Premier League goals for the club and set a new competition record for assists in a single season last term.

Bruno’s comments don’t sound like he is holding United hostage demanding more pay or refusing to sign a new one. The intention as told by Bruno Fernandes just show his leadership trait about putting the team first. He has no immediate intention of making his contract situation the centre of attention. That will be a sign of encouragement for the fans as well.

Manchester United need to start winning games again. When they do and surely Bruno Fernandes will be at the centre of it, the contract talks can resume and take priority.

#2132. Danny Drinkwater on Chelsea move he ‘could never turn down’

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Danny Drinkwater Chelsea story still carries a sting. Five years at Stamford Bridge gave him plenty of time to think about how it all turned out, and his own verdict is not a happy one.

Drinkwater opened up in a Truth or Padel appearance alongside David Ornstein. He said the move was one he could never have turned down, even with the benefit of hindsight. “No, I don’t regret moving. I regret, in hindsight, how it’s turned out. I think I could never turn it down,” he said.

Strip away the headlines and the numbers alone tell an uncomfortable story. Drinkwater spent five years on Chelsea’s books. In that time he made just 23 appearances, according to the original interview report.

Do the maths and it barely comes to five games a year. That is a thin return for a central midfielder signed to compete for a first-team place. It is also the kind of record that rarely sits well at a club of Chelsea’s size and ambition.

Chelsea’s best attacking spells over a similar stretch of seasons look far more productive, as our striker rankings show. Set next to those numbers, Drinkwater’s five quiet years stand out even more starkly.

Five years. Twenty three games. These numbers alone explains why this transfer still gets talked about by Drinkwater, long after the headlines faded.

The numbers only tell part of the story. A string of incidents turned a quiet, underwhelming spell into something far more pointed.

Drinkwater had a training-ground bust-up while out on loan. He was also involved in an on-pitch brawl with Chelsea’s own under-23s side. Flashpoints between a first-team player and a development squad are rare at any club, let alone one with Chelsea’s standards.

Taken alone, either incident might have passed as a bad day. Taken together, it became harder to see Drinkwater simply as an unlucky squad player who could not catch a break.

The most serious moment came during his time at Aston Villa. Drinkwater headbutted team-mate Jota and was fined two weeks’ wages for it. He says the consequences at Chelsea did not stop there.

“They didn’t formally ban me, but I got removed from the first team building after the incident at Villa,” Drinkwater said.

One off-field incident, at another club, pushed him out of the manager’s day-to-day plans back home. No formal punishment at Chelsea followed. The effect was much the same.

Chelsea fans saw a similar breakdown of trust play out when Graham Potter struggled to win over the dressing room during another difficult Chelsea transition. Trust can break down fast once results or behaviour turn against the person at the centre of it.

Drinkwater’s comments matter beyond his own career. They are a reminder that saying yes to a big move does not guarantee it will work once a player walks through the door.

That tension has not gone away. Chelsea’s current transfer business, covered in our transfer watch, shows the club still weighing big calls on players whose futures depend on more than form alone.

Squad management under Xabi Alonso, assessed in our bomb squad verdict, raises a familiar issue. Players who fall outside a manager’s plans rarely find a quick way back in, whether the exile is formal or not.

Drinkwater never found his way back into Chelsea’s plans after the Villa incident. His account of the Danny Drinkwater Chelsea years stands as a blunt warning. A move that looks impossible to refuse can still become one of the hardest spells of a career.

#2131. Why England fans booed Arsenal defender Ben White again after Croatia win

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Ben White returned to the England senior squad on Thursday night but received a hostile reception at Wembley.

The Arsenal defender came on as a substitute in the 78th minute of England’s 2-1 Nations League win against Croatia but was met with boos from a section of the crowd.

Thomas Tuchel has since defended White, stating that he should be in the squad. However, this raises questions as to why some England supporters have turned on the defender after he has continued to perform well for Arsenal.

The answer lies with the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

He did not play in the first two group games for England and missed the last group game against Wales due to illness.

There were reports that White had fallen out with assistant manager Steve Holland, but neither the FA nor England management confirmed this was the reason he left.

Gareth Southgate later stated there were no problems between White and Holland and that White had simply withdrawn himself from selection after the tournament.

This meant that White would never play for England again while Southgate was still manager. Some fans were clearly upset by this, as they felt White was shunning his country.

When White returned under Tuchel in March 2026, he was met with a negative reaction. He was booed by the crowd when he scored his first-ever international goal against Uruguay. White was also booed in the same fashion against Japan.

He has since explained that supporters might view the situation differently if they knew the full story. However, he has chosen not to reveal the private details behind his departure.

Tuchel has shown little concern about White being affected by the controversy.

The England boss said after the win on Thursday that he had not heard any boos and praised White’s qualities, work ethic and desire to play for his country.

He believes White can help England win games and added that he has the backing of the coaching staff.

Arsenal fans will be unsurprised to learn that White is still a valuable asset for Mikel Arteta, offering defensive consistency and being able to play as a right or centre-back.

The bad press that White is receiving from England fans will not go away any time soon. However, he has not done anything to hurt his reputation at club level. The reasons why he left for the World Cup are personal.

The main focus for Arsenal will be getting him match fit again. As for the England fans, we shall see.

#2130. Chelsea sweat on key stars as Bournemouth test looms

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Chelsea return to Premier League action this weekend with a growing treatment table and a lot of questions for Xabi Alonso to answer before Saturday’s visit of Bournemouth.

The main concern revolves around Joao Pedro. Chelsea’s current player of the season rescued a point against newly promoted Hull, but he suffered a knock and sat out the damaging 3-0 defeat at Brentford. The problem also prompted his removal from Brazil’s squad shortly after he had returned to it.

It is understood that he is undergoing specialist knee treatment in an attempt to expedite his recovery, although reports in Brazil suggest that he could be out for up to four weeks. No date has yet been set, but a return later in October looks most likely.

There is more good news elsewhere. Cole Palmer was among the players called up to the latest England squad, which did not go down too well with Thomas Tuchel.

The midfielder has been recovering from a persistent groin injury and has been working with a rehab coach. He is likely to be fit this weekend.

Moises Caicedo has also struggled with an injury this season, playing just 14 minutes across the campaign. He’s spent the majority of time on the bench recovering from a bad calf injury, which ruled him out for most of the season.

He made his only appearance as a substitute against his former club Brighton, but the game was red-flagged for Ecuador’s friendlies, so he did not play.

Alonso said before the Brentford match that the player would be ready to return. It seems to be the case, unless something went wrong.

Captain Reece James missed the Brentford game with yet another hamstring problem. Alonso said he only just missed out, so a return seems likely.

There may also be debuts. Marco Palestra, the £27m signing from Atalanta, has been sidelined since a training injury just before the opening match against Fulham. He is back in full training and was expected to feature in a behind-closed-doors friendly with Portsmouth. Chelsea lost 2-0. Emmanuel Emegha, injured after scoring against Bromley in July, is also pushing for involvement.

Less clear is the position of Jamie Gittens. He limped off with an ankle injury playing for England Under-21s against Kazakhstan and was seen on crutches. Mike Penders is fine after a quad scare on Belgium duty. Returning to the bench against Turkey.

Chelsea badly need a lift. Defeat at Brentford before the break left Alonso’s side looking shaky, and a squad stretched by injuries has not helped.

Saturday brings a chance to steady things. If Palmer, James and Caicedo are available, with Palestra and Emegha potentially adding fresh options, the picture will look much brighter at Stamford Bridge. Joao Pedro’s absence will still sting. However, a strong response against Bournemouth would go a long way towards easing the pressure and restoring belief.

Manchester United players have reportedly been told to expect a further increase in training demands under Mauricio Pochettino after Sunday’s Premier League match against Liverpool.

The new manager arrived at Carrington on Wednesday following his departure from the United States national team and has had less than four days to prepare for his first match in charge. According to The Sun’s report, published on Saturday evening, United’s players have already noticed longer and more intense training sessions compared with those under former manager Michael Carrick.

The newspaper reports that Pochettino has initially concentrated on introducing his tactical approach, with more demanding physical work expected once the Liverpool fixture is over. An unnamed source claimed the players had already felt a significant change in tempo and workload, despite the Argentine having only a limited period to work with the squad.

Pochettino is also reported to have taken a hands-on approach during training, regularly stopping drills to explain his instructions directly to players. The report adds that the 54-year-old has been communicating in English with United’s staff and has asked his predominantly Spanish-speaking coaching team to do likewise.

Pochettino’s first assignment is Sunday’s visit to Anfield, with United looking to improve on a difficult opening to the Premier League season. The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager conducted an extended training session on Saturday as preparations for the fixture continued.

However, the reported emphasis on fitness and conditioning suggests that his wider changes at Carrington may become more apparent after the Liverpool match. United have not publicly confirmed the details of the training programme described in the report.

#2128. Arsenal Women vs London City Lionesses preview: Gunners face tough test at the Emirates

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal look to build on their recent win over Liverpool as they return to the Emirates Stadium but will face an impressive London City Lionesses side who are a potent attacking threat on their travels.

Renée Slegers’ team have struggled to convert their strong performances into points in the league this season. They have lost their last four WSL games at home, however, becoming the first team in WSL history to draw four successive games at home.

Their bad run must come to an end. They have taken just three points from their first nine league games so far this season, scoring a miserable total of 10 goals. However, they look like they have more in the tank and will need to be much more clinical in front of the goal.

The day also marks Slegers’ 50th game in charge of the WSL. The Dutch manager has only lost six league games so far this season, with only Chelsea having a better record from teams that have been ever-present in the division.

Arsenal can’t take their opposition lightly after London City’s impressive recent form. They have won two and drawn once in their last three away league games, scoring 12 goals.

Eder Maestre’s side has become a potent attacking force. Daniëlle van de Donk has provided four assists this season, and Delphine Cascarino has scored three goals and provided two assists.

Kadidiatou Diani can be dangerous. She has scored or assisted in all four of her league games away from home this season.

London City’s attacking prowess means they are a far different proposition to some teams Arsenal have faced at home. They have been in a positive situation for 62.7 per cent of their league minutes this season, the highest in the WSL.

Arsenal will have to deal with the attacking threats but look to utilise their ball possession better. Giving London City an opportunity to counter could make an already tough afternoon even tougher.

Alessia Russo comes into the game having found the net in her last three WSL games and will be key in converting Arsenal’s chances into goals.

The Gunners also showed their fighting spirit in their midweek clash against Barcelona. They drew 1-1 at Camp Nou to become the first side to take points off the Spanish giants in the Women’s Champions League at home since April 2024.

Slegers’ team will feel emboldened by that result but will have to change their tactics against London City.

They have won all seven games against Arsenal so far, scoring an impressive 22 goals and only conceding once. However, given London City’s recent away form, they will be hotly favoured.

They certainly have the quality to take all three points, but they must finally convert their dominance into a comfortable home win.

#2127. Chelsea co-sporting director Laurence Stewart to leave in leadership reshuffle

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club opting to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

The departure is understood to be amicable and won’t take immediate effect. Stewart could continue attending matches before formally leaving, following discussions with co-owner Behdad Eghbali over the club’s evolving sporting structure.

The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.

Stewart arrived from Monaco in October 2022 as technical director before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley in February 2023.

Chelsea’s day-to-day sporting leadership will now be shared between Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields, each with defined responsibilities.

Winstanley will continue overseeing transfer negotiations, player contracts and several departments at Cobham, including medical and performance operations. Shields’ work centres on the academy and player pathways, while Jewell has wider responsibilities across the BlueCo operation, including Strasbourg.

According to Jacobs, discussions about restructuring began in April and accelerated following the appointment of Xabi Alonso as head coach.

Stewart had overseen investment in Chelsea’s data analysis operation, although Jewell and Shields have increasingly taken responsibility for using that information in recruitment and talent identification.

Dave Fallows will remain involved in an advisory capacity, rather than taking on a fixed day-to-day portfolio.

The changes are being described as a natural evolution of Chelsea’s sporting model. There is no suggestion that Stewart’s departure followed a breakdown in relations, and the club are not currently planning to recruit a replacement.

#2126. Scott Parker’s West Ham Striker Admission Leaves Castellanos With A Problem

West Ham United manager Scott Parker has spoken positively about Joël Piroe ahead of Saturday’s Championship clash with Preston North End, raising an interesting question over his starting striker.

During his pre-match press conference, Parker acknowledged the Dutchman’s impressive goalscoring record and revealed that he was looking forward to spending more time working with him.

“I’ve known about Joël, having played against his teams. His goalscoring record is really good,” said Parker.

“It’s a shame for us he’s been away, but he’s in good form, and I’m looking forward to working with him more.”

Personally, I would 100% start Piroe ahead of Taty Castellanos, irrespective of how well the Argentine might have trained during the international break.

Piroe is a proven Championship goalscorer, and Parker knows all about him from his previous experience managing in this division.

I think he very much deserves a run of games in an attempt to fire at least one of our strikers into action.

The alternative is to continue persevering with Castellanos, who has been a considerable disappointment since West Ham’s relegation.

As Claret & Hugh exclusively revealed, the club are exploring the possibility of selling Castellanos in January, with Nils Koppen already investigating potential replacements.

Further reports from Argentina have suggested the striker wants to leave, although no departure has been agreed.

I don’t think there’s any mystery surrounding what Piroe offers.

He knows the Championship, he knows how to score goals in it, and he’s already demonstrated that he can contribute to this West Ham team.

As we’ve previously argued when discussing Parker’s selection options, Piroe has a compelling case to start ahead of Castellanos.

Of course, the manager will have his own ideas about how he wants his centre-forward to play.

But given the lack of goals from our recognised strikers, I’d rather see Parker give the Dutchman a proper opportunity than continue waiting for Castellanos to discover some form.

#2125. Liverpool v Manchester United: Five classic wins at Anfield

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

From Diego Forlan’s unforgettable double to Juan Mata’s spectacular volley, Manchester United have enjoyed some memorable victories at Anfield over the years.

With Mauricio Pochettino preparing for his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday, we look back at five occasions when United emerged victorious from one of English football’s fiercest fixtures.

United travelled to Anfield on 19 April 1997 knowing Liverpool could overtake them at the top of the Premier League with a victory. Instead, centre-back Gary Pallister scored twice with headers from David Beckham deliveries, either side of John Barnes’s equaliser.

Andy Cole added a third after the interval, heading home from Gary Neville’s cross following an error by Liverpool goalkeeper David James. The victory helped Sir Alex Ferguson’s side take a decisive step towards retaining the Premier League title, which they secured the following month.

Fresh from winning the Treble, United returned to Anfield for a remarkable match in September 1999. Jamie Carragher headed into his own net inside three minutes before Andy Cole doubled United’s advantage.

Sami Hyypia pulled a goal back for Liverpool, but Carragher’s second own goal restored the visitors’ two-goal lead. Patrik Berger reduced the deficit again, and United faced a difficult finish after Cole was sent off for a second bookable offence. Despite playing the closing stages with 10 men, Ferguson’s side held on for a 3-2 victory.

Diego Forlan had endured a frustrating start to his United career before producing a performance that supporters would remember for years. The Uruguayan opened the scoring after Liverpool goalkeeper Jerzy Dudek failed to gather the ball, allowing him to finish from close range.

Forlan added a second just minutes later, beating Dudek at his near post to put United in control. Sami Hyypia pulled one back for Liverpool, but Ferguson’s side held on for a victory that proved valuable in their successful pursuit of the 2002-03 Premier League title. Forlan’s double also inspired a terrace song that remains familiar to United supporters.

Few United victories at Anfield have been as dramatic as the one secured by John O’Shea in March 2007. Liverpool had enjoyed the better opportunities, and United’s task became harder when Paul Scholes was sent off late in the second half.

With a goalless draw appearing increasingly likely, Cristiano Ronaldo’s free-kick was parried by goalkeeper Pepe Reina. Substitute O’Shea reacted quickest, firing the rebound high into the net in stoppage time. The unexpected winner gave United three valuable points on their way to reclaiming the Premier League title.

Juan Mata produced one of the most memorable individual performances in this fixture during Louis van Gaal’s first season as United manager. The Spaniard opened the scoring after 14 minutes, finishing a move involving Ander Herrera, before doubling United’s lead with a spectacular scissor-kick volley after half-time.

Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard had been sent off just 38 seconds after coming on as a substitute at the interval. Daniel Sturridge reduced the deficit, while Wayne Rooney missed a late penalty, but United held on for a 2-1 victory. Mata’s second goal remains one of the outstanding moments of United’s Premier League visits to Anfield.

Those five victories underline the different ways United have succeeded at Anfield, from outstanding individual performances to late winners and determined defensive displays. Pochettino now has an opportunity to begin his managerial reign with a memorable result against United’s biggest rivals.

Which United victory at Anfield is your favourite? Were you there for Forlan’s double, O’Shea’s winner or Mata’s volley? Share your memories in the comments below.

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal transfer interest in Alphadjo Cisse is starting to take shape. Arsenal are monitoring the development of AC Milan starlet Alphadjo Cissé, although his sensational start to the season could prove to be costly for Mikel Arteta.

The 20-year-old has made a blistering start to his Serie A career and attracted interest from a number of Premier League clubs after his impressive displays so far. Arsenal are reported to be interested.

The Gunners are among several clubs, including Brighton, keeping tabs on the player, according to Italian football news website Tuttomercatoweb. The striker is rumoured to be worth up to 60 million euros. That’s an eye-watering sum for a player who is just starting out in his professional career.

Cissé was signed by Milan from Hellas Verona in February 2026 but was allowed to finish the season on loan at Catanzaro.

Prior to joining the San Siro, he had already showcased his potential with six goals in 22 games in Serie B. He has made a huge impact since moving up to the top division.

Cissé has found the net five times in nine Serie A games this season. He has also chipped in with three goals in four Europa League games, making a total of eight goals in 13 games.

This has made him an important addition to the Milan squad. He is also versatile, as he can play as an attacking midfielder or higher up the park.

Arsenal may find his versatility attractive. Arteta likes players who can play in different positions and with injuries, and with a busy fixture list, he will want to have players who can do that.

The main issue could be that Milan are keen to keep their young star.

It is reported that the Italian club have turned down a verbal offer from Brighton and are looking to extend Cissé’s contract, which currently runs until June 2030.

This indicates that Milan is considering his future, rather than looking to make a profit. It also demonstrates just how quickly his reputation has developed.

Arsenal have the funds to target exciting young talent, but would they want to spend so much on Cissé?

There is no indication that he would be an instant replacement for Arsenal’s current attacking options. However, Cissé’s age, goal-scoring ability and versatility make him an interesting prospect.

This could be one to keep an eye on beyond January. Milan have little motivation to sell, and Arsenal might want to see how he develops before committing themselves.

Cissé has already hit the ground running in Italy and now needs to prove that his initial success can turn into something more consistent.

#2122. Mark Noble Reveals Important Change Behind West Ham’s Transfer Plans

Mark Noble has provided an interesting insight into how West Ham United’s recruitment operation is working under Scott Parker, revealing that Nils Koppen is in regular contact with the coaching staff about the players the club needs.

Speaking in an interview with West Ham’s official website, Noble explained that the Director of Player Recruitment is arriving at Rush Green as early as 6.30am, watching training and discussing the squad with Parker and his coaches.

With the January transfer window approaching and West Ham desperate to secure promotion, it’s encouraging to hear that recruitment discussions are taking place. But for me, the most important part of Noble’s revelation has very little to do with what time Koppen arrives for work.

Quite frankly, whether Koppen arrives at half six in the morning is neither here nor there.

Much of the analytical and recruitment work can be carried out perfectly well from wherever somebody can plug into the internet.

What I find far more important is the open dialogue Noble has described.

He explained that Koppen watches training and that the coaching staff speak openly with him about the players they believe West Ham need.

Koppen then works with the club’s scouts and analysts in the background, allowing Parker and Noble to concentrate on coaching.

That strikes me as a huge plus and potentially a massive step in the right direction.

It also appears to represent a departure from the way things have operated previously, when questions were regularly raised about whether recruitment decisions matched the manager’s requirements.

As we discussed following Parker’s talkSPORT interview, the manager is absolutely right to concentrate on improving the players already at his disposal rather than becoming consumed by January transfers.

But that only works if the recruitment department understands precisely what he needs.

We know from our recent dialogue with a club insider that Koppen has begun looking for another striker, and Noble’s comments suggest those discussions are taking place alongside the coaching staff’s assessment of the squad.

Ultimately, I’m far more interested in whether Koppen signs the right players than whether he’s the first person through the door at Rush Green.

But if the people coaching the team and those recruiting for it are finally speaking openly about what West Ham need, that has to be encouraging.

Whilst we keep the same coaching staff and listen to their requirements we will continue with our underachieving and bland teams.

We should not be seeking continuity of a failed system. We should be mindful of where we would like to be and how to get there.

Thankful that we are not employing a home worker solely reliant on the internet.

By far the most encouraging article in recent times.

#2121. OLIVER HOLT: Why England CAN now end 62 years of hurt - Thomas Tuchel is intoxicating and I'd tip Jude Bellingham to beat Kylian Mbappe to the next Ballon d'Or... plus my top 10 Three Lions performances

Published: 12:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:04 EST, 16 November 2026

The glum face of Lamine Yamal, head in hands, stared out from the front page of the Spanish sports paper AS as it sat on newspaper stands in Madrid on Monday morning. ‘Fin a la racha,’ the headline said. The end of the run.

For Spain football fans, England’s 3-2 dramatic victory over the world champions in the Spanish capital on Sunday evening made this akin to a day of mourning, the first time their team had tasted defeat in 44 matches, an end to a gilded period of invincibility.

For England, the feeling was very different. Because Sunday night in the cauldron of the Metropolitano felt very much like a beginning. Thomas Tuchel has been the head coach for almost two years but this was the moment of his true arrival.

This was the victory that freed us from looking back to the Groundhog Day pain of that World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in Atlanta last summer and allowed us to look forward to a future that seems luminous and full of hope.

This was the victory that allowed us to stop blaming Tuchel for what happened four months ago and start looking forwards again, dreaming about the glories that he might yet deliver. This was the victory that validated Tuchel and why the FA hired him in the first place. This was the victory that allowed us to believe he might be the Messiah after all.

This felt like the moment when he embraced us, with all our quirks and football idiosyncrasies, and we embraced him. He had promised ‘proof of concept’ on the eve of the game and he delivered it with bells on. Tuchel has harnessed the best of the English game and welded it to his principles and the result is intoxicating.

Thomas Tuchel has harnessed the best of the English game to down world champions Spain

Once you have seen England play the way they did for an hour against Spain, you are lost. You are lost to the belief that the 62 years of hurt might really be coming to an end at Wembley in the final of the European Championship in the summer of 2028. You are lost to the idea that, finally, everything is falling into place.

For the 63 minutes up until the sending off of Elliot Anderson, I have never seen an England performance as good as the one that unfolded in the Metropolitano. Spain are the best team in the world and England outclassed them and stupefied them. They were better than them with the ball and better than them without the ball. They were magnificent.

Because of the context, because of the wonder of the stage, because of the odds they faced, England’s victory over Mexico in the grandeur and the mayhem of the mighty Azteca Stadium during the World Cup might edge Sunday’s performance but for pure football, what England delivered in Madrid demands comparison with the best they have played for many a year.

This year’s World Cup came just too soon but now Tuchel and England understand each other perfectly. And now England are purring. They have a manager who commands the players’ respect and they have a group of players that commands the respect of the manager.

Yes, it was just a Nations League group game but it was against one of the best national sides the world has ever seen. England worked so ferociously and attacked so fluently and defended so devotedly that they reached a level that drew admiration even from their opponents.

Many, many things will live long in the memory. James Trafford’s miraculous double save in the dying minutes gets better every time I watch it. Ben White’s goal channels the beauty of Carlos Alberto’s strike for Brazil against Italy in the 1970 World Cup Final, too. Let’s hope that strike, and his superb defensive performance, bring an end to the boos that have been his companion of late.

Jude Bellingham was relentless, tireless and glided through the game against Spain

Tuchel had promised ‘proof of concept’ on the eve of the game and he delivered it

And then there was Jude Bellingham. Just when you think you can’t admire him any more than you do, he delivers a performance like the one he produced against Spain, a performance that lifted him above even the exalted company of the other players on two fine teams.

Bellingham was tireless. He was relentless. He glided past challenges. He thundered into tackles. He dominated midfield. He has the heart and the sheer brilliant indomitability that Bryan Robson possessed.

Bellingham has it in him to be England’s greatest ever player. He needs trophies to fulfil that destiny but maybe, finally, trophies are in reach again.

He has the team around him to do it, which Robson never quite had. Jordan Pickford is a good goalkeeper but Trafford might just be better. Ezri Konsa had his best game for England in Spain. White and Lewis Hall were superb at full back. Little more needs to be said about England’s front six. They are as good as any unit in world football.

Harry Kane, of course, was the best player in the world last year. Some seem to assume that the Ballon d’Or will inevitably pass to Yamal or Kylian Mbappe next. I think it is more likely to be Bellingham.

The man is a colossus. He is a footballer who has everything. He does not know how to be beaten.

Bellingham saw off Barcelona rival Lamine Yamal - and could beat him to the Ballon d'Or

With them together, the sky is the limit. And Bellingham has also proved to be a player of immense mental strength. It was not so long ago that people worried about his discipline but the fortitude he showed when he was being targeted by Argentina at the World Cup was the best answer to that.

He and Kane are England’s axis of ambition on the pitch. Tuchel is lucky to have them and they are lucky to have him, too. The coach has reached the point where his tactics and his team-building are bearing fruit.

Now England have a team-manager package that genuinely need fear nobody. The victory against Spain was a rehearsal for the bigger stage of major tournaments. Going down to 10 men after 63 minutes against the best team in the world might not have been in the script but that is what rehearsals are for.

After Sunday night in the Metropolitano, England are ready for their close-up.

#2120. Chelsea’s interest in Alex Scott remains despite Bournemouth transfer stance

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. Bournemouth’s determination to keep Alex Scott has done little to discourage Chelsea, who remain among the leading contenders to sign the England midfielder.

The Blues had a £64m bid rejected during the summer, but their interest has continued into the new season. According to Matt Law of The Telegraph, Chelsea are at the front of the queue of clubs monitoring the 23-year-old.

Bournemouth, however, have no intention of allowing Scott to leave in January. talkSPORT reported this week that the south coast club remain determined to retain him, despite his reluctance to sign a contract extension.

Scott’s current deal runs until 2028, leaving Bournemouth with time to negotiate, although their position could become more complicated if no agreement is reached before next summer.

The midfielder’s immediate priority is recovering from a thigh injury sustained while representing England. He impressed during the 7-0 Nations League victory over Croatia but was withdrawn after 70 minutes. Subsequent examinations revealed a quadriceps problem, with BBC Sport reporting that he could miss six to eight weeks.

His absence is a setback for Bournemouth, who have relied heavily on the former Bristol City midfielder this season. It also introduces another consideration for clubs monitoring his progress ahead of the January window.

Chelsea are not alone in their admiration. Arsenal and Liverpool have also been linked with Scott, whose performances have attracted attention beyond the Premier League.

Suggestions circulating on social media that Bournemouth have already agreed to let him leave in January remain unsubstantiated. There has been no reliable confirmation of such an arrangement, and the club’s reported position is firmly against a winter sale.

For Chelsea, the more realistic opportunity may come next summer, particularly if Scott continues to resist signing a new contract.

#2119. Max Dowman breaks Jude Bellingham record as Arsenal teenager makes England history

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Max Dowman has added another incredible achievement to his burgeoning career after becoming the youngest player to play for the England Under-21s.

The Arsenal youngster was introduced from the bench in Friday’s 1-0 friendly loss to Portugal at Ashton Gate. The 16-year-10-month-13-day-old player is over three months younger than Jude Bellingham was when he played his first game for the Under-21s.

Dowman replaced former Arsenal academy player Amario Cozier-Duberry in the 61st minute. He came on alongside debutant Trey Nyoni as England tried to shift the momentum of a challenging game.

An early strike from Afonso Moreira gave Portugal the lead in the 28th minute. An ineffective England team failed to respond. However, the replacements gave Lee Carsley’s team some late momentum.

Despite the hosts’ attempts to level the score, they failed to break down the Portuguese defence. The result means England have lost for the second game running. However, Dowman had much to be pleased with personally.

Dowman has added to his growing collection of records.

He became the youngest player to play in the Champions League, the youngest goalscorer in the history of the Premier League and the youngest to win the Premier League title.

Breaking Bellingham’s England Under-21 record is another significant step. It shows how quickly Dowman has progressed through the international age groups.

He has already made a big impression at Arsenal with Mikel Arteta’s love of giving younger players a chance, but Dowman will have some stiff competition for first team minutes.

Another positive is his progression on an international scale. He will improve both physically and tactically playing against older players and gain experience at a higher level.

England will host France in their next friendly on Monday, 16th November. Dowman will be hoping to feature after his instant impact on the record books.

Despite the disappointing result against Portugal, it was a landmark evening for the Arsenal players.

Dowman is already building a legacy at club level, but now he can add to his list of records by becoming an England Under-21 record holder.

At just 16, he has plenty of time to improve and show consistent performances to get more opportunities with the senior Arsenal squad.

#2118. Simple: Scott Parker’s secret weapon in West Ham reboot

West Ham return to action tomorrow with a home tie against visitors Preston North End – a team who sit rock bottom of the Championship but are not without their recent triumphs after turning over promotion-chasing Southampton just before the break. So West Ham need to be wary, despite their opponents’ lowly league table position.

With Scott Parker having enjoyed an unbroken two week training period during the break, West Ham fans will now surely get to see the ‘Parker XI’ rather than Nuno’s inherited lin-up with which he began the first two games of his West Ham tenure.

The first visible difference will surely be to see -shock, horror – players used in their correct positions: Nuno because infamous for using square pegs in round holes – Morato at left back being the case in point.

Morata’s days at left back are surely over

Despite being signed as a centre back and having played all but 33 of his last 177 games as such, Nuno insisted on using the 6’3 Brazilian – hardily the most mobile – as a left back who was frequently found to be out of position, often allowing wingers to get the better of him: Scott Parker hooked him at half time after a pretty inept left-back performance against Cardiff.

With centre back Maximilian Kilman suspended for tomorrow’s clash there should be no more Morato at left back – incredibly West Ham fans have never seen the loanee in his preferred specialist position until now. Ezra Mayers has already done enough to start at left back leaving Parker free to slot Morato into the role for which he was signed, alongside Mavropanos.

Square pegs into square holes: Scott Parker’s secret weapon in his West Ham reboot. Who’d have thought.

Chelsea have reportedly made contact with Palmeiras as they attempt to gain an early advantage in the race to sign Brazilian teenager Eduardo Conceicao.

The 16-year-old forward has attracted attention from several leading European clubs, but Chelsea are understood to be among the first to establish direct contact with Palmeiras over a potential future transfer.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, the London club have held a series of discussions as they seek to position themselves ahead of their rivals.

Palmeiras are reportedly preparing for substantial offers, with some figures at the Brazilian club discussing a valuation as high as €100m (£85m).

That figure has not been established as a firm asking price, however, and Brus reports that industry sources expect the eventual cost to be lower. Chelsea’s previous investment of approximately £51m in Estevao is regarded as a possible benchmark.

Manchester City’s ownership group have also made contact regarding Conceicao, while Arsenal, Manchester United, Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain are among the clubs reported to have watched him.

Chelsea’s existing relationship with Palmeiras could help their efforts, although the level of competition means there is no guarantee that their early interest will lead to a deal.

The player’s age is another consideration. Conceicao cannot complete an international transfer to England until he turns 18, leaving interested clubs facing a potentially lengthy wait before he can join their squads.

Chelsea have already demonstrated their willingness to agree deals for young players well before they are eligible to arrive, with Estevao providing a particularly relevant example.

No formal bid or agreement has been reported for Conceicao. Nevertheless, the latest claims suggest Chelsea are prepared to explore another long-term investment in Brazilian talent rather than wait until the player becomes available for an immediate move.

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Martin Ødegaard has spoken out about the speculation surrounding his future. He has stated he would like to stay at Arsenal for the future.

The captain has also admitted that talks about a new deal have not yet begun. Ødegaard is currently under contract until the summer of 2028. This leaves Arsenal with an important decision to make over the coming months.

Bayern Munich are being linked with an interest in the midfielder according to reports from Germany. The Bundesliga giants are said to be keeping their eyes on the player’s situation.

Speaking while on international duty with Norway, Ødegaard was quick to dismiss the speculation. He made it clear he is settled in north London and sees his future being at the Emirates Stadium.

There is no suggestion that the 27-year-old is seeking a move. Although comments do highlight a contract issue that Arsenal will be keen to resolve in the short term.

The Norwegian’s laid-back attitude should be encouraging for supporters.

He has made it clear that he is happy at the club and wants to stay here for the time being. This means that there is no need to panic.

However, Arsenal will have to get him to sign on the dotted line. Leaving his captain in the last year of his contract with no progress would cause an unnecessary distraction.

Since his permanent move from Real Madrid in 2021, Ødegaard has become a key player in Mikel Arteta’s plans. He has grown into a team leader and is one of the most influential players in the dressing room.

His importance has been shown by his inclusion in all 10 of Arsenal’s Premier League games so far this season. He has scored three goals.

This is a big improvement on last season, where he was hampered by injuries and failed to make much of an impact in front of goal.

It wouldn’t be a shock to see Bayern Munich show interest in Ødegaard, but don’t take this as a sign he is close to a move.

There is little reason for Arsenal to consider losing their captain. He brings so much more to the team than just his technical ability and has been relied upon by Arteta to lead by example.

The midfielder was also pivotal in the 1-0 win over Hull City on 7 November, scoring the winner in the 72nd minute to give the league leaders three crucial points.

Arsenal have put themselves in a good position in the title race. Keeping their key players happy will be important in the second half of the campaign.

The Gunners will be focused on their game against Newcastle United on 21st November.

Arsenal fans have no real reason to panic at the moment, with the captain wanting to stay at the club and his comments suggesting he is happy.

However, it would be a good idea for the club to try and ensure his long-term future at the club. Ødegaard is still an important part of Arteta’s strategy, and ensuring he stays at the club would be a smart move.

#2115. Chelsea news: Stewart departure, Scott interest and Bournemouth preparations

Chelsea’s sporting department is facing another change following news of Laurence Stewart’s impending departure, while the club continue to be linked with potential additions to their squad.

Alex Scott and Palmeiras teenager Eduardo Conceicao have both featured in Thursday’s transfer coverage, with Xabi Alonso also preparing his players for Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth.

Here is our 7pm round-up of the latest Chelsea news for Thursday, 8 October.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club planning to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

His departure is understood to be amicable and will not take immediate effect. Stewart joined from Monaco in 2022, initially as technical director, before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley.

As detailed in our report on Stewart’s departure and Chelsea’s leadership reshuffle, Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields are expected to take on expanded responsibilities across recruitment, player development and the wider BlueCo operation.

The changes follow discussions about the club’s sporting structure that reportedly began earlier this year. There is no confirmed suggestion that Stewart’s departure resulted from a disagreement with Alonso.

Chelsea’s reported interest in Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott remains a talking point, despite the south coast club’s determination to retain the England international.

The Blues reportedly had a £64m offer rejected during the summer, with Matt Law of The Telegraph subsequently identifying Chelsea as leading contenders for the 23-year-old.

However, as examined in our latest report on Chelsea’s interest in Scott, Bournemouth are not expected to entertain a January sale.

Scott’s immediate concern is recovering from a thigh injury suffered while representing England. The midfielder could face several weeks on the sidelines, potentially complicating Bournemouth’s plans as well as any future discussions about his next move.

Chelsea have also reportedly made contact with Palmeiras over 16-year-old forward Eduardo Conceicao, who is attracting attention from several leading European clubs.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, Chelsea have held discussions with the Brazilian club as they explore the possibility of a future deal.

Our report on Chelsea’s interest in Eduardo Conceicao explains that a valuation as high as €100m has been suggested, although that figure is not a confirmed asking price or evidence of a formal bid.

Manchester City, Arsenal and Real Madrid are among the other clubs reportedly monitoring the teenager. Conceicao would be unable to complete a transfer to England until he turns 18, making any prospective move a longer-term consideration.

Alonso’s attention will now turn to Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge.

The match kicks off at 3pm and will not be televised live in the United Kingdom because of the Saturday afternoon broadcasting blackout.

Our Chelsea v Bournemouth kick-off and how-to-watch guide provides the full details, including how to follow the match and the available overseas broadcast information.

Scott’s injury is expected to deprive Bournemouth of an important midfield option, although Chelsea will have their own fitness decisions to make as players return from international duty.

After Saturday’s fixture, Chelsea travel to Hill Dickinson Stadium to face Everton on 17 October. Alonso will be looking for greater consistency as the domestic programme resumes.
